items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: Does the Biometric & Attendance Policy apply to me?
items.a: Yes, if you work from the office. It applies to all employees working from office, except those who work from home, work in the field, or are specifically approved by management for an exception.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: I work from home. Do I have to punch biometric attendance?
items.a: No. The policy excludes employees who are working from home with management approval.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: I am a field employee. Do I need to follow biometric attendance?
items.a: No. Employees working from the field are excluded from this policy.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: Who decides whether I can be excluded from biometric attendance?
items.a: Management. Only employees specifically approved by management (apart from WFH and field staff) are excluded.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: Why does the company have an attendance policy?
items.a: To make sure everyone is at work on time every business day so that daily business runs smoothly and workplace practices stay fair and consistent.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: Is attendance management mandatory?
items.a: Yes. The policy states that attendance management is mandatory under labour laws, and not following it leads to non-compliance.

items.s: Who Does This Policy Apply To?
items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. Management can change, amend or withdraw any or all conditions of the policy at any time, without prior intimation.

items.q: When will my biometric be enrolled after I join?
items.a: All new joiners are enrolled on their second day of joining.

items.q: Where will my biometric enrollment happen?
items.a: At the Prahladnagar/Nehrunagar office.

items.q: I joined today. Can I get enrolled on the same day?
items.a: As per the policy, enrollment is done on the second day of joining, not on the first day.

items.q: Is the biometric system linked to my salary?
items.a: Yes. The biometric attendance system is synchronized directly with payroll to fetch attendance and calculate salary.

items.q: Can my salary be affected by my punching record?
items.a: Yes. Because biometric data feeds payroll, shortfalls in working hours or missing punches can result in half-day or full-day LWP (LOP) deductions.

items.q: Do I have to clock in and clock out every day?
items.a: Yes. You must clock in at your entry time and clock out at your exit time according to your work schedule (shift timing).

items.q: What is "clock in" and "clock out"?
items.a: Clock in means recording your entry on the biometric system when you start work. Clock out means recording your exit when you leave.

items.q: How much lunch time do I get?
items.a: 30 to 45 minutes is given for lunch.

items.q: Do I need to clock out for lunch?
items.a: The policy does not require clock-out for the 30-45 minute lunch break. It only says lunch time of 30-45 minutes is given.

items.q: When do I need to clock out during the day?
items.a: Whenever you leave the office premises for more than 20 minutes for non-work-related matters, you must clock out.

items.q: I am stepping out for 10 minutes to the tea stall. Do I need to clock out?
items.a: No. Clock-out is required when you leave the premises for more than 20 minutes for non-work matters.

items.q: I am going out for 45 minutes for a personal errand. What should I do?
items.a: Clock out when you leave, since it is more than 20 minutes and non-work related, and clock in when you return.

items.q: I am going out for an official meeting. Do I clock out?
items.a: The clock-out rule applies to non-work-related matters. For official travel, submit an On Duty Request in GreytHR with your manager's approval.

items.q: What is my entry time?
items.a: Your entry time depends on your work schedule or shift timing. Please check with your manager or HR for your exact shift.

items.q: Can I change my shift timing on my own?
items.a: No. You are expected to follow the schedule assigned to you. Any change should go through your manager and HR.

items.q: Do I need to clock out at the end of the day?
items.a: Yes. You must clock out at the end of your workday.

items.q: What happens if I forget to clock in or clock out?
items.a: Inform your reporting manager immediately and update your attendance in GreytHR for approval. Employees who consistently fail to clock in or out may receive a warning letter and loss of pay.

items.q: I forgot my punch only once. Will I get a warning letter?
items.a: A warning letter is for employees who consistently fail to clock in or out. A one-time miss should be reported to your manager and regularized.

items.q: Is clock-in and clock-out mandatory for each shift?
items.a: Yes. Employees must clock in and clock out for each shift.

items.q: The biometric machine did not work when I tried to punch. What do I do?
items.a: Update your attendance in GreytHR and inform your manager immediately for approval.

items.q: Who approves my attendance if the biometric had a technical glitch?
items.a: Your reporting manager approves it.

items.q: Do I need to tell my manager if the machine had a glitch, or only update GreytHR?
items.a: Both. You need to update GreytHR and also inform your manager immediately.

items.q: Can I tell my manager about the glitch next week?
items.a: No. The policy says to inform the manager immediately.

items.q: Does a technical glitch count in my 2 monthly regularizations?
items.a: The policy treats glitch updates as a separate process (update GreytHR and get manager approval). It does not say it is counted in the 2 regularizations. Please confirm with HR if unsure.

items.q: How many hours do I need to work to be marked present for a full day?
items.a: 8 hours 30 minutes (8.30 hours) is calculated as a full day present.

items.q: How many hours make a half day present?
items.a: 4 hours of working is calculated as a half day present.

items.q: I worked less than 4 hours. How will my day be counted?
items.a: Anything less than 4 hours is considered a full day absent.

items.q: I worked 6 hours. What will my attendance be?
items.a: Since it is more than 4 hours but less than 8.30 hours, it will be counted as a half day absent (half day present).

items.q: I worked exactly 4 hours. Is that a half day?
items.a: Yes. 4 hours is calculated as a half day present.

items.q: I worked 8 hours 15 minutes. Is that a full day?
items.a: No. A full day needs 8.30 hours. Anything less than 8.30 hours but more than 4 hours is a half day absent.

items.q: I came 10 minutes late but stayed late too. Is it a full day?
items.a: The day is counted by total working hours. If your total hours reach 8.30, it is a full day present.

items.q: Does the lunch break count in my working hours?
items.a: The policy does not say how lunch is treated in the hour calculation. Please check with HR.

items.q: What happens if I am marked half day?
items.a: A half day LWP (LOP) is deducted subject to the punching record.

items.q: What happens if I am marked absent due to less than 4 hours?
items.a: A full day LWP (LOP) is deducted subject to the punching record.

items.q: Will deduction happen for both late arrival and early exit?
items.a: Attendance is calculated by total hours worked. If your hours fall short of 8.30 (or 4), the half-day or full-day deduction applies.

items.q: Are employees expected to follow office timings strictly?
items.a: Yes. Employees are expected to adhere to office timings.

items.q: What is attendance regularization?
items.a: It is a correction of your attendance record in GreytHR for a small shortfall, such as late arrival or early exit.

items.q: How many times can I regularize my attendance in a month?
items.a: Maximum 2 times in a month.

items.q: How much shortfall can be regularized?
items.a: The shortfall must not exceed two hours per instance.

items.q: I am short by 3 hours. Can I regularize?
items.a: No. Regularization is only allowed when the shortfall is two hours or less per instance.

items.q: I did not use my regularizations this month. Can I use 4 next month?
items.a: No. Unused regularization is not carried forward to the next month.

items.q: I have used my 2 regularizations. Can I regularize a third time?
items.a: No. The maximum is 2 per month. Beyond that, your attendance will be treated as per the working-hour rules (half day or full day LOP) unless you apply for leave.

items.q: I punched only once (only check-in). Can I regularize?
items.a: No. For a single punch, the day is not eligible for regularization. You must apply for a full-day leave.

items.q: I forgot to punch out. Can I use regularization?
items.a: A single punch (only check-in or only check-out) is not eligible for regularization. You must apply for a full-day leave.

items.q: Where do I regularize my attendance?
items.a: In the GreytHR portal.

items.q: Do I need my manager's approval for regularization?
items.a: Yes. You must keep your immediate reporting manager informed, and the attendance update goes for manager approval.

items.q: What if I am late for a genuine reason?
items.a: It is your duty to inform your immediate reporting manager about the late arrival and regularize your attendance in GreytHR.

items.q: Is there a limit on how many times I can be late?
items.a: The policy limits regularization to 2 times a month. Repeated lateness beyond that may lead to LOP and disciplinary action.

items.q: If I regularize, will I still lose pay?
items.a: If the shortfall is regularized within the policy limits, the deduction for that instance is not applied.

items.q: I need to travel for office work. What should I do?
items.a: Submit an On Duty Request through GreytHR and get it approved by your reporting manager before you go.

items.q: Can I apply On Duty after returning from the trip?
items.a: No. The request must be approved by your reporting manager before proceeding with the travel.

items.q: Who approves my On Duty Request?
items.a: Your reporting manager.

items.q: Is an On Duty Request required for every official outside visit?
items.a: The policy requires it for any employee intending to travel outside for official purposes.

items.q: What happens if I travel without an approved On Duty Request?
items.a: Your day may show as an absence or shortfall in the biometric record, which is linked to payroll, and LOP could be applied. Always get approval first.

items.q: How do I report that I will be absent?
items.a: Report the absence through the GreytHR application.

items.q: I am unwell today and cannot come. What should I do?
items.a: Inform your manager and apply for the appropriate leave in GreytHR promptly.

items.q: How soon should I apply for leave after an unplanned absence?
items.a: Promptly, within a reasonable period of time. If you do not, LOP will be applied for those days.

items.q: What if I don't give any information about my leave?
items.a: It will be considered as Loss of Pay.

items.q: I was absent but did not apply for leave. Will I get paid?
items.a: No. If there is no information about the leave, it is treated as Loss of Pay.

items.q: My manager has not approved or rejected my leave. What happens?
items.a: As per the policy, if the reporting manager takes no action on the leave, the manager's LWP will be considered for not taking any action.

items.q: Does the manager have a duty to act on leave requests?
items.a: Yes. Managers must take action on their employees' leave requests.

items.q: Do I need to inform HR about an absence?
items.a: Report through GreytHR and keep your reporting manager informed. HR can also be informed as per the Leave Policy.

items.q: I am absent for 3 days continuously. What do I need to provide?
items.a: If you are absent for three or more consecutive days, you must provide evidence to excuse the absence, such as a doctor's note.

items.q: What happens if I do not provide evidence for 3+ days of absence?
items.a: It will be considered as job abandonment or termination without notice.

items.q: What kind of evidence is accepted?
items.a: A doctor's note is given as an example. Other valid supporting documents may be shown to your manager and HR.

items.q: Can I get an exception for a long absence?
items.a: Employees may request exceptions for extended work absences from their respective managers. These are approved case by case.

items.q: Who approves exceptions for extended absence?
items.a: The reporting manager approves on a case-to-case basis.

items.q: What disciplinary action can happen for attendance issues?
items.a: Progressive disciplinary action, which includes loss of pay and warning letters, and in serious cases job abandonment or termination.

items.q: What is "progressive disciplinary action"?
items.a: It means action that increases step by step with repeated or serious attendance issues.

items.q: When can I receive a warning letter?
items.a: When you consistently fail to clock in or clock out.

items.q: Can attendance issues lead to termination?
items.a: Yes. Absence of 3 or more consecutive days without evidence can be treated as job abandonment or termination without notice.

items.q: Is attendance policy compliance linked to labour laws?
items.a: Yes. The policy says attendance management is mandatory under labour laws.

items.q: I came late because of traffic. What should I do?
items.a: Inform your reporting manager and regularize the attendance in GreytHR, within the limit of 2 times per month and 2 hours per instance.

items.q: I left early for a doctor's appointment. How is it treated?
items.a: If you do not complete 8.30 hours, it is a half-day LOP (if over 4 hours). You can regularize if the shortfall is within 2 hours and you have a regularization left, or apply for leave.

items.q: I worked from home for one day due to an emergency. Will it count?
items.a: Only management-approved WFH is excluded from biometric. Take your manager's approval and ensure attendance is updated in GreytHR.

items.q: Do I need to punch on a weekly off?
items.a: The policy does not require a punch on a weekly off. If your supervisor asks you to work on a weekly off, your presence and hours are verified by HR for Comp Off.

items.q: Can my colleague punch for me?
items.a: No. The policy requires every employee to clock in and clock out themselves for their own shift. Please do not ask anyone to punch for you.

items.q: I work in a different shift. Which timing applies to me?
items.a: Your own work schedule or shift timing applies.

items.q: What if I have a half-day leave approved and work 4 hours?
items.a: A half-day leave plus a half-day present (4 hours) is counted as a full working day.

items.q: Where can I check my attendance record?
items.a: In GreytHR.

items.q: Who do I contact if my attendance looks wrong in payroll?
items.a: Inform your reporting manager and HR, and raise it in GreytHR before payroll closes.

items.q: Is attendance data used to calculate my salary every month?
items.a: Yes. Biometric data is synchronized with payroll to calculate attendance and salary.

items.q: Is a reminder given before LOP is applied?
items.a: The policy does not mention any reminder. Apply for leave or regularize promptly to avoid LOP.

items.q: Does the 2-times-a-month regularization limit apply to every employee?
items.a: Yes, it applies to all employees covered by this policy (office employees).

items.q: If I regularize twice in a month, will my attendance for those days be full day?
items.a: Yes, if the regularization is approved and each shortfall is within two hours, those days are regularized.

items.q: Can I regularize a half-day shortfall of 4 hours?
items.a: No. A shortfall of more than two hours per instance cannot be regularized. The day will be treated as a half day or full day LOP as per the hours rule.

items.q: Who do I inform if the reason for lateness is genuine?
items.a: Your immediate reporting manager.

items.q: Do I have to inform HR as well when I am late?
items.a: The policy requires informing your immediate reporting manager and regularizing in GreytHR. HR is not named in this step.

items.q: What does "LWP" mean in the policy?
items.a: LWP means Leave Without Pay. It is the same as LOP (Loss of Pay).

items.q: Is LOP applied automatically?
items.a: Yes. Because attendance is synchronized with payroll, LOP is applied based on the punching record unless leave or regularization is approved.

items.q: If I am marked half-day absent, can I apply a half-day leave to cover it?
items.a: You can apply for the appropriate leave through GreytHR, subject to the Leave Policy and your manager's approval.

items.q: Is single punch a common reason for LOP?
items.a: Single punch days are not eligible for regularization, so you must apply for a full-day leave. Otherwise, LOP will apply.

items.q: Can I get exemption from clocking in on a particular day?
items.a: Only management can approve exceptions. Talk to your manager and HR in advance.

items.q: What if my manager is on leave and cannot approve my regularization?
items.a: Inform HR so that your attendance can be approved by the appropriate authority, since a pending action may otherwise lead to LOP.

items.q: Will repeated late coming be treated as misconduct?
items.a: Attendance issues result in progressive disciplinary action, so repeated late coming can lead to warning letters and loss of pay.

items.q: Is job abandonment only for 3-day absence?
items.a: The policy mentions job abandonment where an employee is absent for three or more consecutive days and does not provide evidence.

items.q: Where can I read this policy again?
items.a: Ask HR or check the policy section on the company HR portal or GreytHR.

items.q: What is a Compensatory Off (Comp Off)?
items.a: A Comp Off is a day off given in return for working on a public holiday or weekly off.

items.q: Why does the company have a Comp Off policy?
items.a: So that employees who are asked to work on a holiday or weekly off get a day of rest in return.

items.q: Who can get a Comp Off?
items.a: An employee who is asked by their supervisor to work on a public holiday or weekly off.

items.q: Is Comp Off my right whenever I work on a holiday?
items.a: No. It is allowed only when your supervisor or HOD requests you to work on the holiday or weekly off.

items.q: Where does this policy apply?
items.a: It applies to working on public holidays or weekly offs when requested by the supervisor.

items.q: I want to come on Sunday to finish my work. Can I get a Comp Off?
items.a: No. You cannot decide on your own to work on a holiday or weekly off and then ask for Comp Off.

items.q: My supervisor verbally asked me to come on Saturday. Is that enough?
items.a: No. The supervisor/HOD must inform you in advance and mark a copy to hr@petpooja.com with approval and a short justification.

items.q: Who can request me to work on a weekly off?
items.a: Your supervisor or HOD.

items.q: Can a colleague (not my supervisor) ask me to work on a holiday and give me Comp Off?
items.a: No. Only your supervisor/HOD can request it with a copy to HR.

items.q: Can I refuse to work on a holiday?
items.a: The policy does not mention refusal. It says supervisors should use discretion and minimize such instances so employees get weekly rest. Please discuss with your supervisor.

items.q: Why does HR need to be copied?
items.a: So HR can verify your presence on that day and confirm that the request was approved in advance.

items.q: What email ID should my supervisor copy for Comp Off requests?
items.a: hr@petpooja.com.

items.q: What should the supervisor's email contain?
items.a: Advance intimation to the employee, approval for working on the holiday or weekly off, and a short justification.

items.q: Can my supervisor ask me to work on holidays regularly?
items.a: Supervisors are advised to use discretion and minimize Comp Off requirements so that employees get rest every week.

items.q: How many hours must I work to earn a half-day Comp Off?
items.a: A minimum of 4 hours.

items.q: How many hours must I work to earn a full-day Comp Off?
items.a: A minimum of 8.30 hours.

items.q: I worked 3 hours on a Sunday as asked. Will I get Comp Off?
items.a: No. The minimum for even a half-day Comp Off is 4 hours.

items.q: I worked 6 hours on a holiday. What do I get?
items.a: A half-day Comp Off, since you did more than 4 hours but less than 8.30 hours.

items.q: I worked 8 hours on a weekly off. Do I get a full day?
items.a: No. A full day Comp Off needs a minimum of 8.30 hours. You will get a half day.

items.q: I worked 9 hours on a weekly off. Do I get a full day Comp Off?
items.a: Yes. You worked more than 8.30 hours, so you get 1 day of Comp Off.

items.q: I worked 12 hours. Do I get 2 days Comp Off?
items.a: No. The policy gives 1 day for 8.30 hours or more. It does not give extra Comp Off for additional hours.

items.q: How are my working hours verified?
items.a: HR verifies your presence on the day, based on attendance records.

items.q: Do I need to punch in and out on the holiday?
items.a: Yes, it is advisable. HR verifies your presence and hours from the attendance record.

items.q: How many Comp Offs can I earn in a month?
items.a: Maximum 3 Comp Offs in a month.

items.q: How many Comp Offs can I take in a month?
items.a: A maximum of 3 Comp Offs can be availed in a month.

items.q: I worked on 4 weekly offs in a month. Will I get 4 Comp Offs?
items.a: No. You can earn a maximum of 3 Comp Offs in a month.

items.q: Can I earn Comp Off for half days and combine them?
items.a: The policy gives half-day Comp Off for 4 hours and full-day for 8.30 hours, subject to the limit of 3 per month.

items.q: Does the 3 per month limit apply to earning and taking both?
items.a: Yes. You can earn up to 3 and avail up to 3 in a month.

items.q: I have 3 Comp Offs and want to take all together for a long weekend. Is that okay?
items.a: Yes, you may avail up to 3 in a month, subject to your manager's approval.

items.q: Can I take 4 Comp Offs in one month if I have a balance?
items.a: No. The maximum is 3 availed in a month.

items.q: How long is my Comp Off valid?
items.a: As per the policy, it is valid till the end of the next month (30 days), after which it expires.

items.q: What happens if I do not use my Comp Off within validity?
items.a: It lapses automatically. No compensation is given for lapsed Comp Offs.

items.q: Can I get cash for an unused Comp Off?
items.a: No. Unused Comp Offs lapse and no further compensation is given.

items.q: Can I carry forward my Comp Off to the next year?
items.a: No. The policy does not allow it. Comp Off expires after the validity period.

items.q: I earned a Comp Off in January. Until when can I use it?
items.a: It is valid until the end of the next month, so you should use it by end of February.

items.q: I earned a Comp Off on the last day of the month. Is it still valid until the next month end?
items.a: Yes, it is valid until the end of the following month.

items.q: Will I be reminded before my Comp Off expires?
items.a: The policy does not say. Please track your Comp Off balance and use it on time.

items.q: If I resign, what happens to my Comp Off?
items.a: The policy says unavailed Comp Offs lapse and no further compensation is given.

items.q: If some of my Comp Offs lapsed, will all of them lapse?
items.a: The policy note says that if Comp Off accumulation is not availed within the particular period, all Comp Offs accumulated during that period lapse automatically.

items.q: I worked on a company-declared public holiday for a full day. Do I get Comp Off?
items.a: No. You get one extra day of salary for that day, and no Comp Off is provided.

items.q: What counts as "full day" for extra salary on a public holiday?
items.a: Working a full day on the company-declared public holiday. The policy refers to the 8.30 hours full day standard.

items.q: Do I get extra pay if I work on a weekly off?
items.a: No. For weekly off, you get Comp Off, not extra salary.

items.q: Do I get Comp Off for working on a public holiday?
items.a: No. For a company-announced public holiday worked for a full day, you get one extra day of salary instead.

items.q: What if I worked only half day on a public holiday?
items.a: The extra day salary is for working a full day. For less than a full day, please check with HR as the policy does not specify.

items.q: Which holidays qualify for extra salary?
items.a: Public holidays announced by the company, excluding weekly offs.

items.q: Is extra salary paid in the same month?
items.a: The policy does not specify. It will be processed through payroll as per HR process.

items.q: Is a Saturday/Sunday weekly off treated as a public holiday?
items.a: No. Weekly off and public holiday are treated differently. Weekly off gives Comp Off; announced public holiday gives extra one day salary.

items.q: How do I apply for Comp Off?
items.a: Apply through the leave system (GreytHR/HRMS) after your Comp Off is credited, with your manager's approval.

items.q: Do I need approval to take a Comp Off day?
items.a: Yes. Please take approval from your reporting manager like any other leave.

items.q: Can I attach a Comp Off to my other leaves?
items.a: This is allowed with manager approval, subject to the monthly limit of 3 Comp Offs.

items.q: Can my manager reject my Comp Off request?
items.a: Business needs may affect approval. Please plan and use it well before expiry.

items.q: Can I use Comp Off during notice period?
items.a: The Separation Policy says no leave is allowed in notice period except exceptional cases with approval. Please check with your manager and HR.

items.q: Can I use a Comp Off to cover a day of LOP?
items.a: Please check with HR. The policy does not specify this.

items.q: Can I use half-day Comp Off?
items.a: Yes. A half-day Comp Off is earned for working at least 4 hours.

items.q: What if my supervisor asks me to come and I do not turn up?
items.a: HR verifies attendance. The policy says the supervisor will also be held accountable if records show that an employee expected to work on a holiday did not turn up.

items.q: Is the employee responsible if he skips a requested holiday duty?
items.a: The employee may face questions from the supervisor and HR. The supervisor is also held accountable as per the policy.

items.q: What if my supervisor forgets to copy HR?
items.a: Without the advance email with a copy to HR, your Comp Off may not be approved. Ask your supervisor to send it on time.

items.q: Can the approval be taken after I worked?
items.a: No. The approval must be given in advance.

items.q: Can I forward the supervisor's email to HR myself?
items.a: The policy requires the supervisor/HOD to mark a copy to HR. Please ask your supervisor to do it.

items.q: Does the policy encourage supervisors to call employees on holidays?
items.a: No. Supervisors are advised to minimize Comp Off requirements so employees can rest every week.

items.q: Our team has a release on Sunday. My manager told us verbally. What should we do?
items.a: Ask the manager to send an email to the team with a copy to hr@petpooja.com with a justification, before Sunday.

items.q: I came on Sunday for 5 hours without being asked. Will I get Comp Off?
items.a: No. You cannot decide to work on your own and then claim Comp Off.

items.q: I was asked to work 4 hours on Saturday. What Comp Off will I get?
items.a: Half-day Comp Off.

items.q: I worked 2 weekly offs in a month for 8.30 hours each. How many Comp Offs do I get?
items.a: 2 Comp Offs (1 day each).

items.q: I worked on 3 Sundays for 4 hours each. How much Comp Off do I get?
items.a: 3 half-day Comp Offs, which is 1.5 days.

items.q: I worked on a company holiday (full day) and my manager says take Comp Off. Is that right?
items.a: No. As per the policy, you get one extra day's salary for a full day worked on an announced public holiday, and no Comp Off.

items.q: Can I claim both extra salary and Comp Off for a public holiday?
items.a: No. The policy says Comp Off will not be provided for that day.

items.q: Can an intern get Comp Off?
items.a: This policy does not mention interns. Please check with HR.

items.q: Is travel time counted in the hours?
items.a: The policy counts hours worked. Please check with HR for travel time.

items.q: Does working from home on a weekly off count?
items.a: HR verifies presence on the day, so please get it approved by your supervisor and HR in advance.

items.q: My team is working on a public holiday that is optional. Do I get extra pay?
items.a: Extra pay applies to company-announced public holidays. For optional holidays, please check with HR.

items.q: Who tracks my Comp Off balance?
items.a: HR and the leave system. You can also check your balance on the portal.

items.q: What if my Comp Off is not credited?
items.a: Contact HR with the advance email, and attendance records for the day.

items.q: I want a comp off.
items.a: You can get a Comp Off only if your supervisor/HOD asked you in advance (with a copy to hr@petpooja.com) to work on a holiday or weekly off, and you worked at least 4 hours (half day) or 8.30 hours (full day).

items.q: How many comp offs do I have?
items.a: Check your balance in the leave portal. Remember you can earn a maximum of 3 per month, and each expires after its validity.

items.q: What is the minimum time I need to work to get any Comp Off?
items.a: 4 hours.

items.q: Can I get Comp Off for working 4 hours 30 minutes?
items.a: Yes, a half-day Comp Off, since you worked at least 4 hours but less than 8.30 hours.

items.q: Can I get Comp Off for working 8 hours 29 minutes?
items.a: You will get a half-day Comp Off, because a full day needs a minimum of 8.30 hours.

items.q: Is Comp Off given for night shift or late-evening work on a working day?
items.a: No. Comp Off applies only to work on public holidays or weekly offs.

items.q: Is Comp Off given if I work late on a normal working day?
items.a: No. It applies only to public holidays and weekly offs.

items.q: Does a supervisor need to give a reason for calling me on a holiday?
items.a: Yes. The supervisor/HOD must give a short justification in the email to HR.

items.q: Who is accountable if I do not show up on a holiday I was asked to work?
items.a: The supervisor is also held accountable, and HR will verify the records.

items.q: Who verifies that I actually worked on the holiday?
items.a: HR.

items.q: Are Comp Offs encashable?
items.a: No. Unused Comp Offs lapse and no compensation is paid.

items.q: I earned 3 Comp Offs this month and worked on one more weekly off. What happens?
items.a: You can earn a maximum of 3 Comp Offs in a month, so the fourth will not be credited.

items.q: What does "validity till end of next month" mean?
items.a: A Comp Off earned in a month must be used by the end of the following month, after which it expires.

items.q: Can I use a Comp Off in the same month I earned it?
items.a: Yes, subject to your manager's approval and the limit of 3 Comp Offs availed per month.

items.q: Can my supervisor give me Comp Off without informing HR?
items.a: No. HR must be informed in advance with approval and a short justification.

items.q: Does Comp Off apply to optional holidays?
items.a: The policy mentions public holidays and weekly offs. Please check with HR for optional holidays.

items.q: What is the benefit if I work on a company-announced public holiday?
items.a: If you work a full day, you get one extra day's salary for that day.

items.q: Do I get a Comp Off if I work on a company-announced public holiday for half a day?
items.a: The policy only mentions extra day's salary for a full day. Please confirm with HR for a half day.

items.q: Is the extra day's salary equal to my regular daily salary?
items.a: The policy says "extra one day salary". HR calculates it as per payroll rules.

items.q: Is working on a holiday compulsory when my supervisor requests?
items.a: The policy says employees may be required to work on off days when the supervisor requests. Supervisors are advised to minimize such requests.

items.q: Can I swap my weekly off with another day instead of Comp Off?
items.a: The policy does not mention swapping. It only provides Comp Off for working on weekly off.

items.q: Will lapsed Comp Offs be restored if I was on leave and could not use them?
items.a: The policy says they lapse and no further compensation is given. Any exception needs HR approval.

items.q: Can I request HR to extend the validity of my Comp Off?
items.a: The policy does not provide extension. You may talk to HR in a genuine case, but approval is not guaranteed.

items.q: What happens to accumulated Comp Offs if I am absent for long?
items.a: If not availed within the period, they lapse automatically.

items.q: Does Comp Off count as paid leave?
items.a: Yes, it is a day off in lieu of the day you worked, so no salary is deducted for that day.

items.q: Does the 3-per-month limit include half-day Comp Offs?
items.a: The limit is on the number of Comp Offs. Please check with HR on how half days are counted.

items.q: Can I apply for Comp Off on GreytHR?
items.a: Comp Off is managed through the leave/attendance system. Please check with HR for the exact option in GreytHR.

items.q: I worked on a weekly off but my supervisor did not mail HR. Can I still claim?
items.a: It is not eligible as per the policy because advance intimation and a copy to HR are required. Ask your supervisor and HR to check.

items.q: What is the Employee Professional Development Support Policy?
items.a: It is a policy under which Petpooja gives financial support to employees for professional development courses, to build their skills and knowledge.

items.q: Why does the company offer this support?
items.a: To help employees grow personally and professionally, which also contributes to the company's success.

items.q: Will the company pay for my course?
items.a: Petpooja can cover part of the course fee if you meet the eligibility criteria and get approval. It is not guaranteed.

items.q: Is this support a contractual right?
items.a: No. The policy does not create a contractual obligation for Petpooja to provide financial support for any course.

items.q: Can the company change or stop this policy?
items.a: Yes. The company reserves the right to modify or discontinue the policy at any time.

items.q: Am I eligible for course fee support?
items.a: You are eligible if you are a full-time confirmed employee who has completed at least one year in the company, the course is related to your role, it is from a recognized provider and your Department Head approves.

items.q: I joined 8 months ago. Can I apply?
items.a: No. You need to complete at least one year in the company.

items.q: I have completed one year but I am still on probation. Can I apply?
items.a: No. You must be a confirmed employee. Both full-time confirmed status and one year of service are required.

items.q: I am a confirmed employee with 1 year and 1 month of service. Am I eligible?
items.a: Yes, on service and confirmation. The course must also meet the other conditions and be approved by your Department Head.

items.q: I am a part-time employee. Can I apply?
items.a: No. The policy is for full-time confirmed employees.

items.q: I am a contract employee. Can I apply?
items.a: The policy is for full-time confirmed employees. Please check with HR for contract staff.

items.q: Can an intern apply for this support?
items.a: No. Only full-time confirmed employees with at least one year of service are eligible.

items.q: Which kind of course is eligible?
items.a: A course directly related to your current role or a position you are being groomed for within the company.

items.q: I want to learn something completely different from my job. Will the company support it?
items.a: No. The course must be directly related to your current role or the position you are being groomed for.

items.q: Can I do an MBA with company support?
items.a: It is possible only if it is directly related to your role or the position you are groomed for, offered by a recognized institution, and approved by your Department Head and HR. The cap on support still applies.

items.q: Can I take a course from any online platform?
items.a: The course must be offered by an accredited institution or a recognized training provider.

items.q: What is a recognized training provider?
items.a: A reputed training body or institution recognized in the industry. Please check with HR before enrolling if you are unsure.

items.q: Who must approve my course?
items.a: Your Department Head, and HR also reviews the proposal.

items.q: Can my reporting manager approve instead of my Department Head?
items.a: The policy requires approval by the Department Head.

items.q: Does the course have to be directly linked to my job?
items.a: Yes, directly related to your current role or a position you are being groomed for.

items.q: What does "groomed for a position" mean?
items.a: A future role the company is preparing you for, as discussed with your Department Head.

items.q: How do I apply for course fee support?
items.a: Submit a written proposal to your Department Head and the HR department.

items.q: What should be in the proposal?
items.a: The course content, how it is relevant to your role, and the expected benefits to the company.

items.q: Who reviews my proposal?
items.a: The Department Head and HR.

items.q: On what basis is my proposal approved?
items.a: On the course's relevance to your role and its potential impact on your performance and career development.

items.q: What do I submit after approval?
items.a: A copy of the course enrollment confirmation and the fee structure to the HR department.

items.q: Can I enroll in the course before getting approval?
items.a: You should wait for approval first. The approval is based on the proposal, and documents are submitted after approval.

items.q: How long does the approval take?
items.a: The policy does not specify the time. Please follow up with your Department Head and HR.

items.q: What if my proposal is rejected?
items.a: The decision is based on relevance and impact. You can discuss feedback with your Department Head and HR and reapply with a stronger proposal.

items.q: Is a verbal request enough?
items.a: No. A written proposal is required.

items.q: Do I need to send the proposal to both HR and my Department Head?
items.a: Yes, to both.

items.q: Can I apply for more than one course at once?
items.a: The policy allows support once in two years. So only one course can be sponsored in that period.

items.q: How much will the company pay for my course?
items.a: Up to 50% of your monthly gross salary or Rs. 50,000, whichever is lower.

items.q: My gross salary is Rs. 60,000. What is the maximum support?
items.a: 50% of Rs. 60,000 is Rs. 30,000. Since it is lower than Rs. 50,000, the maximum support is Rs. 30,000.

items.q: My gross salary is Rs. 1,50,000. What is the maximum support?
items.a: 50% would be Rs. 75,000, but the cap is Rs. 50,000. So the maximum is Rs. 50,000.

items.q: My gross salary is Rs. 1,00,000. What is the maximum support?
items.a: 50% is Rs. 50,000, which equals the cap. So the maximum is Rs. 50,000.

items.q: My gross salary is Rs. 40,000. What is the maximum support?
My gross salary is Rs. 80,000. What is the maximum support?
Is the 50% calculated on my CTC or my gross salary?
items.a: On your monthly gross salary.

items.q: What does the support cover?
items.a: Course fees, including tuition fees and any required materials.

items.q: Does the support cover travel or accommodation?
items.a: No. The policy covers course fees (tuition and required materials) only.

items.q: Does it cover exam fees?
items.a: The policy mentions tuition fees and required materials. Please check with HR for exam or certification fees.

items.q: My course fee is Rs. 1,00,000. How much will I pay?
items.a: Support is limited to the lower of 50% of your monthly gross salary or Rs. 50,000. The remaining amount must be paid by you.

items.q: Does the company pay the entire course fee?
items.a: No. Only up to the limit mentioned in the policy.

items.q: Is the support given as a loan?
items.a: No, it is financial support. But it may have to be repaid if you leave before the committed period.

items.q: Is the support taxable?
items.a: The policy does not mention tax. Please check with HR or Finance.

items.q: How will the payment be made?
items.a: Payment is made directly to the educational institution after receiving the invoice.

items.q: I have already paid the fees. Can I get a reimbursement?
items.a: Yes. Reimbursement will be processed after the course is completed and you submit proof of payment and satisfactory completion.

items.q: When will I get my reimbursement?
items.a: After completion of the course and submission of proof of payment and satisfactory completion.

items.q: Can I get reimbursement before the course finishes?
items.a: No, if you paid yourself. Reimbursement happens after completion with the required proof.

items.q: What proof of payment is required?
items.a: A receipt or other proof of payment of the fees.

items.q: Will the institution get the amount if I submit the invoice?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja pays directly to the institution upon receipt of the invoice.

items.q: Who do I give the invoice to?
items.a: The HR department.

items.q: What do I need to submit after completing the course?
items.a: Proof of completion such as a certificate or transcript, to HR.

items.q: What if I do not complete the course?
items.a: You must successfully complete it. Without completion proof, reimbursement may not be processed, and repayment may be asked in some cases.

items.q: What if I fail the course?
items.a: You must successfully complete the course. Please discuss with HR; the policy needs satisfactory completion for reimbursement.

items.q: Do I need to give any presentation after the course?
items.a: You may be required to submit a brief report or presentation to your HOD and HR on how the course benefited your role and the company.

items.q: Is the report or presentation mandatory?
items.a: It is "may be required". Your HOD or HR can ask for it.

items.q: Who evaluates the benefits from the course?
items.a: Your HOD and HR.

items.q: Do I have to stay in the company after the course?
items.a: Yes. You are expected to stay at Petpooja for at least one year after completing the course.

items.q: What if I resign before completing one year after the course?
items.a: You may be required to repay 75% of the course fees paid by the company.

items.q: My course cost the company Rs. 40,000 and I resign in 6 months. How much do I repay?
items.a: You may have to repay 75% of Rs. 40,000, which is Rs. 30,000.

items.q: If I had paid some fee myself, will I repay that too?
items.a: No. The repayment is of the course fee paid by the company.

items.q: How will the repayment be recovered?
items.a: The company can deduct the amount from your final settlement (FnF).

items.q: The policy mentions "pro-rated repayment" and also "75% repayment". Which one applies?
items.a: The policy says failure to stay may result in a pro-rated repayment, and also says you may be required to repay 75%. The exact amount will be confirmed by HR.

items.q: Does the one-year commitment start from the course start date or the completion date?
items.a: From the completion of the course.

items.q: Does the commitment apply if I am terminated?
items.a: The policy mentions resignation. For any other case, please check with HR.

items.q: Do I need to sign a bond?
items.a: The policy talks about an employment commitment. Please check with HR if a separate agreement is required.

items.q: What if I leave after one year and one day of completing the course?
items.a: You will not be required to repay under this policy, since you fulfilled the one-year commitment.

items.q: How often can I avail this support?
items.a: After you avail it once, you become eligible again after two years.

items.q: I used this support in 2024. When can I apply again?
items.a: After two years, so from 2026 onwards.

items.q: Can I apply every year?
items.a: No. The gap between two supports is two years.

items.q: Is the two-year gap counted from the course start or completion?
items.a: The policy only says an employee who has availed the benefit is eligible again after two years. Please confirm the start point with HR.

items.q: I want to do a Digital Marketing certification and I work in marketing. Is it eligible?
items.a: It may be eligible if the course is from a recognized provider, related to your role, and approved by your Department Head and HR.

items.q: I am in the sales team and want to do a coding course. Will it be approved?
items.a: Only if it is directly related to your current role or a position you are being groomed for.

items.q: My Department Head has approved, but HR has not. What now?
items.a: The proposal is reviewed by both. Please check with HR on the pending point.

items.q: Can I apply for a course which has already started?
items.a: The policy asks for a proposal and approval first. Enrolling before approval is risky.

items.q: Can I get approval for a course that is also self-funded by me?
items.a: You can apply for a part-support up to the policy limit. Please check with HR for how to apply.

items.q: Can I apply when I am on notice period?
items.a: The post-course commitment of one year makes it unlikely. Please discuss with HR.

items.q: I am under a Performance Improvement Plan. Can I apply?
items.a: The policy does not mention it, but the Department Head approval is needed. Please discuss it with your Department Head.

items.q: Who is the contact for questions on this policy?
items.a: The HR department.

items.q: I want to do a course. What should I do first?
items.a: Check that you have completed one year as a confirmed full-time employee, then submit a written proposal to your Department Head and HR with course content, relevance and benefits.

items.q: Am I eligible for course support?
items.a: If you are a full-time confirmed employee with at least one year in the company, and the course is related to your role and from a recognized provider, you can apply with your Department Head's approval.

items.q: How much support can I get?
items.a: Up to 50% of your monthly gross salary or Rs. 50,000, whichever is lower.

items.q: Will the company pay the institution directly?
items.a: Yes, on receipt of the invoice, payment is made directly to the institution.

items.q: Do I need to give my course certificate to HR?
items.a: Yes. Proof of completion such as a certificate or transcript must be given to HR.

items.q: Can I get support for a course my friend recommended on a random website?
items.a: Only if it is offered by an accredited institution or recognized training provider and is related to your role.

items.q: Does a probationer get this support?
items.a: No. Only full-time confirmed employees with at least one year of service.

items.q: Is the one-year service counted from my date of joining?
items.a: Yes, you must have completed at least one year in the company.

items.q: What happens to the support if my Department Head changes?
items.a: Approval is by the Department Head, so a new Department Head may need to review it. Please speak to HR.

items.q: Is the support given for each course separately?
items.a: Support can be availed once, and you become eligible again after two years.

items.q: Do I need to pay the rest of the fee myself?
items.a: Yes. The company covers only up to the policy limit, and the rest is paid by you.

items.q: Can I take leave to attend my course?
items.a: The policy does not cover leave. Please take your manager's approval as per the Leave Policy.

items.q: Can the course be during working hours?
items.a: The policy does not say. Please discuss with your Department Head.

items.q: What if the course fee is less than 50% of my salary?
items.a: The company may support up to the actual fee, within the policy limit.

items.q: Can I get the support for a PhD or long-term degree?
items.a: The cap applies, and approval is based on role relevance. Please discuss with your Department Head and HR.

items.q: Can the company ask me to return the money if I leave after one year?
items.a: No. The repayment applies if you resign before completing one year after the course.

items.q: Do I need to show satisfactory performance in the course?
items.a: Yes. Reimbursement needs proof of payment and satisfactory completion.

items.q: Who decides if my course benefited the company?
items.a: Your HOD and HR, who may ask for a brief report or presentation.

items.q: What documents do I need for reimbursement?
items.a: Proof of payment, proof of satisfactory completion (certificate or transcript), and the enrollment confirmation and fee structure.

items.q: Can I apply again if my first request was rejected?
items.a: Yes. A rejection does not mean you have availed the benefit, so you may reapply with a stronger proposal.

items.q: What is the Relocation Expense Reimbursement Policy?
items.a: It explains who is eligible for reimbursement of moving expenses when the company requires an employee to relocate for business needs, and how to claim it.

items.q: Which company issued this policy?
items.a: Prayosha Food Services Private Limited (Petpooja).

items.q: Why does the company have this policy?
items.a: To support employees who must relocate to meet the company's evolving needs or to take new opportunities.

items.q: Will the company pay if I decide to shift my house myself?
items.a: No. Employees who propose their own relocation are not eligible for any reimbursement.

items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. HR may review and revise the policy periodically at its discretion.

items.q: Who is eligible for relocation reimbursement?
items.a: Full-time Petpooja employees with at least three years of continuous service, where the relocation is initiated and directed by the company and pre-approved.

items.q: I have 2 years of service. Am I eligible?
items.a: No. You need a minimum of three years of continuous service.

items.q: I have exactly 3 years of service. Am I eligible?
items.a: Yes, on service. The relocation must also be company-initiated and pre-approved.

items.q: Does "continuous service" mean without any break?
items.a: Yes. The three years must be continuous at Petpooja.

items.q: I am a part-time employee. Can I claim?
items.a: No. The policy applies only to full-time employees.

items.q: I am a contract employee. Can I claim?
items.a: The policy applies only to full-time employees. Please check with HR for contract staff.

items.q: Is an intern eligible?
items.a: No. Only full-time employees with three years of continuous service are eligible.

items.q: I am on probation. Can I claim relocation expenses?
items.a: No. Three years of continuous service are required.

items.q: What does "initiated and directed by the company" mean?
items.a: The company must be the one that asks you to move for business needs. If you ask to move for personal reasons, it is not covered.

items.q: I requested a transfer to another city for personal reasons. Do I get reimbursement?
items.a: No. Self-proposed relocation is not eligible.

items.q: My manager suggested that I move to another city and I agreed. Is that company-initiated?
items.a: It must be initiated and directed by the company and pre-approved by the department head or Management/HR in writing.

items.q: Who needs to approve my relocation?
items.a: The appropriate Department Head or Management/HR.

items.q: When should the approval be taken?
items.a: Before relocation. The relocation must be pre-approved to be eligible.

items.q: Can I get approval after I shift?
items.a: No. The policy requires pre-approval.

items.q: What do I need to submit for approval?
items.a: A written request outlining the reasons and relevant supporting documentation.

items.q: Is a verbal request enough?
items.a: No. You must submit a written request.

items.q: What should I write in the relocation request?
items.a: The reasons for the relocation and supporting documents, such as the company's relocation direction and quotations.

items.q: Who do I send my request to?
items.a: To your Department Head and Management/HR for pre-approval.

items.q: Is approval guaranteed if I meet all the conditions?
items.a: The policy says the relocation must be pre-approved. Approval is at the discretion of the department head or Management/HR.

items.q: How many times can I claim relocation reimbursement?
items.a: Only once during your tenure.

items.q: I claimed in 2022. Can I claim again if the company relocates me again?
items.a: No. Reimbursement is allowed only once during an employee's tenure.

items.q: Does the one-time limit apply even if the move is to a different city?
items.a: Yes. The limit is once in your entire tenure.

items.q: What expenses are covered?
items.a: Reasonable and necessary moving expenses of the employee and immediate family, such as transportation, packing and shipping of household goods.

items.q: Are my family's expenses covered?
items.a: Yes, for immediate family members.

items.q: Are household goods transport costs covered?
items.a: Yes. Transportation, packing and shipping of household goods are covered.

items.q: Is there a maximum limit?
items.a: Yes. Rs. 30,000 maximum reimbursement.

items.q: My movers charged Rs. 45,000. How much will I get?
items.a: Maximum Rs. 30,000. You will bear the rest.

items.q: My movers charged Rs. 25,000. How much will I get?
items.a: Up to Rs. 25,000, based on approved quotation and actual invoice, within the Rs. 30,000 cap.

items.q: Are travel and hotel expenses covered?
items.a: Yes. Reasonable travel and hotel expenses for you and your immediate family during relocation are reimbursed with a total cap of Rs. 5,000.

items.q: Is the Rs. 5,000 travel cap in addition to the Rs. 30,000?
items.a: Yes. The policy lists Rs. 30,000 for moving expenses and a separate total cap of Rs. 5,000 for travel and hotel expenses.

items.q: Does the Rs. 5,000 cap apply per person?
items.a: No. It is a total cap for the employee and immediate family members.

items.q: Is rent for the new house covered?
items.a: No. The policy covers moving expenses, travel and hotel only.

items.q: Is the security deposit for the new house covered?
items.a: No. It is not mentioned in the policy.

items.q: Are broker charges covered?
items.a: No. They are not mentioned in the policy.

items.q: Is vehicle transportation (bike or car) covered?
items.a: The policy mentions household goods. Please check with HR for vehicles.

items.q: Are packing material charges covered?
items.a: Yes, packing is covered as part of moving expenses, subject to the cap and quotation.

items.q: Are pets covered?
items.a: Not mentioned in the policy. Please check with HR.

items.q: Are food expenses during relocation covered?
items.a: Only reasonable travel and hotel expenses are mentioned. Please check with HR for food.

items.q: What are "immediate family members"?
items.a: The policy does not define it in detail. It generally means spouse, children and dependent parents. Please confirm with HR.

items.q: How many quotations do I need?
items.a: Three different quotations from certified movers and packers.

items.q: When do I submit the quotations?
items.a: Before relocation approval.

items.q: Which quotation will the company consider?
items.a: The lowest quotation.

items.q: Can I choose the costlier vendor?
items.a: You can, but reimbursement will be based on the lowest quotation, subject to the Rs. 30,000 cap.

items.q: Can I choose any packer and mover?
items.a: They must be certified movers and packers.

items.q: Who selects the vendor?
items.a: The employee is responsible for selecting the vendor and coordinating the move.

items.q: What if the actual cost exceeds the approved quotation?
items.a: You will pay the difference.

items.q: The vendor increased the price after the quotation was approved. Who pays the extra?
items.a: You. The employee is fully responsible for paying the difference.

items.q: Can I get a revised quotation approved?
items.a: The policy does not provide for it. You are responsible to ensure the move happens within the approved quotation.

items.q: Can I submit fewer than three quotations?
items.a: No. Three different quotations are needed.

items.q: Can the three quotations be from the same vendor?
items.a: No. They must be from different certified movers and packers.

items.q: When will I be reimbursed?
items.a: After successful relocation and submission of the required documents.

items.q: What documents do I need to submit?
items.a: Final invoice, payment proof, and approved quotations.

items.q: Will the company pay in advance?
items.a: No. The policy provides reimbursement after relocation.

items.q: Who processes the reimbursement?
items.a: HR and the accounts team, as per the standard process.

items.q: Is there a time limit to submit claims?
items.a: The policy does not specify one. Submit as soon as possible after the move.

items.q: Do I need original bills?
items.a: A final invoice and payment proof are required. Please submit originals or valid copies as required by Accounts.

items.q: Will the reimbursement be paid with salary?
items.a: The policy does not say. It is processed after document submission.

items.q: What if I resign after relocation?
items.a: If you resign within one year following the relocation date, the full reimbursed amount will be deducted from your Full and Final settlement.

items.q: What if I am terminated after relocation?
items.a: If you are terminated within one year following the relocation date, the full reimbursed amount will be deducted from your Full and Final settlement.

items.q: How much will be recovered, in full or partial?
items.a: The full reimbursed amount.

items.q: I resigned 13 months after relocating. Do I repay?
items.a: No. The recovery applies only within one year of relocation.

items.q: Does the one-year period start from the date I submit the claim?
items.a: No. It starts from the relocation date.

items.q: Is the Rs. 5,000 travel reimbursement also recovered?
items.a: The policy says the full reimbursed amount will be deducted, which includes all reimbursements under this policy.

items.q: Will I get leave for relocation?
items.a: Yes. Leave taken during relocation is treated as paid leave, subject to approval by your reporting manager and Department Head.

items.q: How many days of leave can I get?
items.a: A maximum of 3 working days.

items.q: Do I need to use my own leave balance?
items.a: No. It is considered paid leave, subject to approval. You do not need to use Casual or Privilege Leave.

items.q: Can I take 5 days off for relocation?
items.a: Only 3 working days are allowed as relocation leave. The rest must be applied as other leave.

items.q: Can I take leave without approval?
items.a: No. Approval of your reporting manager and Department Head is required.

items.q: Is relocation reimbursement taxable?
items.a: Employees are responsible for understanding and complying with the tax implications. The company may offer general guidance.

items.q: Will the company pay my tax on this amount?
items.a: No. The employee is responsible for tax implications.

items.q: Who can I ask about the tax impact?
items.a: The policy recommends seeking independent tax advice. HR may also provide general guidance.

items.q: The company is moving me from Ahmedabad to another city. What steps should I follow?
items.a: Get written pre-approval, collect three quotations from certified movers, finalise the lowest, relocate, and submit the final invoice, proof of payment and the quotations.

items.q: I moved first and want to submit bills later. Will it be paid?
items.a: No. Pre-approval and quotations are required before relocation.

items.q: Can I claim a flight ticket for my family?
items.a: Reasonable travel expenses are included within the total travel and hotel cap of Rs. 5,000.

items.q: Can I claim both movers' bill and my own car fuel?
items.a: Fuel is not specifically mentioned. Reasonable travel may be claimed within the Rs. 5,000 cap.

items.q: I used a local transport company that is not certified. Can I claim?
items.a: The policy requires quotations from certified movers and packers.

items.q: Does the company bear the extra amount if the quotation is lower than the actual cost?
items.a: No. The employee pays the difference.

items.q: What if my relocation was cancelled after approval?
items.a: The policy does not cover this. Please inform HR immediately.

items.q: What if my department head changes before the move?
items.a: Please get the approval reconfirmed in writing by the new department head or HR.

items.q: Whom can I ask for questions about relocation?
items.a: HR and your Department Head.

items.q: Is this policy only for Petpooja or also for subsidiaries?
items.a: It applies to full-time employees of Petpooja (Prayosha Food Services Private Limited).

items.q: I want relocation money.
items.a: You are eligible only if you have completed 3 years of continuous service, the company directed your relocation, and you got written pre-approval. Then you can claim up to Rs. 30,000 for moving and Rs. 5,000 for travel and hotel.

items.q: What is the total I can claim under this policy?
items.a: Up to Rs. 30,000 for moving expenses plus up to Rs. 5,000 for travel and hotel, i.e. Rs. 35,000 in total.

items.q: Can I get reimbursement if I relocate on my own to a nearby city?
items.a: No. Only company-directed relocation is covered.

items.q: Is the policy only for out-of-city moves?
items.a: The policy says relocation required by business needs. Please check with HR for within-city moves.

items.q: Do I need to take pre-approval from HR or my Department Head?
items.a: From the appropriate Department Head or Management/HR.

items.q: Will I get paid leave even if the company is not paying for my move?
items.a: The paid leave of up to 3 working days applies to relocation under this policy, with approval.

items.q: What happens if the move costs less than the approved quotation?
items.a: You are reimbursed the actual expense on the final invoice, within the approved quotation and the cap.

items.q: What if I want to move after 6 months of approval?
items.a: The policy does not set a validity period. Please confirm the timing with HR.

items.q: Is shipping of household goods by courier or transport allowed?
items.a: Yes. Transportation, packing and shipping of household goods are covered.

items.q: Can my spouse's expenses be claimed?
items.a: Yes, as an immediate family member.

items.q: Can I claim for my parents moving with me?
items.a: Immediate family members are covered. Please check with HR on the definition.

items.q: What if I leave within 1 year? Will I need to repay the paid leave also?
items.a: The policy mentions deduction of the reimbursed amount. The paid leave is not a reimbursement.

items.q: Who is responsible if the movers damage my goods?
items.a: The employee selects and coordinates with the vendor. The policy does not provide for damage claims.

items.q: Does the company provide a relocation allowance beyond these limits?
items.a: No. The maximum reimbursement limits in the policy are Rs. 30,000 and Rs. 5,000.

items.q: What is IJT?
items.a: IJT stands for Internal Job Transfer. It lets an employee move to a new role within the organization.

items.q: Why does the company have this policy?
items.a: To give employees opportunities to explore new roles, build skills and contribute to the organization's growth.

items.q: Who can apply for IJT?
items.a: Employees who meet the service, performance and conduct criteria in the policy.

items.q: Where can I read the IJT policy?
items.a: From the HR department or the company policy folder. HR can also answer your questions.

items.q: Does the company treat every eligible employee equally in IJT?
items.a: Yes. Selection is based on skills, qualifications and performance rather than personal bias.

items.q: I want to move to a different department at the same level. When can I apply?
items.a: If it is in the same VP's team, you must complete 6 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: I want to move to a department under a different VP. When can I apply?
items.a: You must complete 18 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: I joined 7 months ago. Can I apply for IJT to a department under the same VP?
items.a: Yes, since you have completed more than 6 months, provided you meet the other conditions.

items.q: I joined 7 months ago. Can I apply to a department under a different VP?
items.a: No. You need 18 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: I have completed 12 months. Can I apply to a different VP's department?
items.a: No. You need 18 months.

items.q: I have completed 18 months in my department. Can I apply to any department?
items.a: You can apply to a different department with the same designation level under a different VP, provided you meet performance and conduct conditions.

items.q: What does "same designation level" mean?
items.a: The new role must be at the same level as your current designation.

items.q: Can I apply for a higher designation through IJT?
items.a: The policy mentions IJT to a different department with the same designation level. A promotion is a separate matter handled in appraisal.

items.q: Do the 6 or 18 months count from my joining date?
items.a: They count from the time you have been in your current department and designation.

items.q: I changed my designation 4 months ago in the same department. Can I apply?
items.a: You need to complete 6 months (or 18) in your current department and designation. Please confirm your date with HR.

items.q: Can I apply for IJT in my probation period?
items.a: The policy does not specifically say. Practically, you need 6 months in the role, and performance and standing must be satisfactory. Please check with HR.

items.q: I already moved through IJT once. Can I apply again?
items.a: Yes, after completing 18 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: Do I need 18 months again even if the second move is in the same VP's team?
items.a: Yes. After a successful IJT, you can apply again only after 18 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: What performance level is required?
items.a: Satisfactory or above expectations in your current role.

items.q: I have a "needs improvement" rating. Can I apply?
items.a: No. Your performance should be satisfactory or above.

items.q: What does "good standing" mean?
items.a: That you have no conduct or compliance issues and you meet the qualifications for the desired position.

items.q: I got a warning letter 4 months ago. Can I apply?
items.a: No. There should be no formal disciplinary action in the past six months.

items.q: I got a warning letter 8 months ago. Can I apply?
items.a: Yes, if you meet the other conditions. The restriction is for formal disciplinary action within the past six months.

items.q: Does a verbal warning count as formal disciplinary action?
items.a: The policy mentions "formal disciplinary action". Please check with HR on how your case is treated.

items.q: I am on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). Can I apply?
items.a: Your performance must be satisfactory or above, so it is unlikely. Please speak to HR.

items.q: Do I need to meet the job requirements of the new role?
items.a: Yes. You must meet the qualifications and requirements of the desired position.

items.q: Who confirms that my performance is satisfactory?
items.a: HR and your current manager based on performance records.

items.q: How will I know about open positions?
items.a: Internal job openings are communicated through email.

items.q: How do I apply?
items.a: Submit your application through the Klimb platform.

items.q: What should I include in my application?
items.a: Your reasons for seeking a transfer and how your skills align with the desired position.

items.q: Can I apply by email instead of Klimb?
items.a: No. The policy requires the application through the Klimb platform.

items.q: Do I need my current manager's permission to apply?
items.a: The policy does not require it for applying, but managers collaborate on transition if you are selected. Confidentiality applies to the process.

items.q: Can I apply for more than one position?
items.a: The policy does not restrict it. If your application is unsuccessful, you cannot reapply for any position for 3 months.

items.q: Can I apply when no opening is announced?
items.a: No. IJT happens against internal job openings communicated through email.

items.q: I did not receive the email about the opening. What should I do?
items.a: Contact HR to confirm if the position is open and to be added to the internal mailing.

items.q: How will I be selected?
items.a: HR screens applications, qualifications and skills are assessed, and interviews are done by the hiring manager and relevant team members. Selection is on merit.

items.q: Who does the first screening?
items.a: The HR team.

items.q: Will there be an interview?
items.a: Yes. Interviews and evaluations are done by the hiring manager and relevant team members.

items.q: Is selection guaranteed if I am eligible?
items.a: No. Selection is based on merit and alignment with the job requirements.

items.q: Will my friends in the team influence my selection?
items.a: No. Selection is based on skills, qualifications and performance, not personal bias.

items.q: Is the IJT process confidential?
items.a: Yes. All employees involved must maintain confidentiality of application details, selection discussions and other sensitive information.

items.q: Can I tell my teammates that I applied for IJT?
items.a: You should keep the application details confidential.

items.q: What happens if I am selected?
items.a: Your current and new managers will plan a transition together.

items.q: Can I decline the offer after accepting the IJT transfer letter?
items.a: No. Once you accept the IJT Transfer Letter you cannot decline the offer and go back to your previous role.

items.q: Can I decide after I see the transfer letter?
items.a: Think carefully before accepting. After acceptance you cannot return to your earlier role.

items.q: Can I return to my old role if I don't like the new one?
items.a: No. After accepting the IJT Transfer Letter, you cannot decline and return.

items.q: What if I am not selected?
items.a: You cannot reapply for the same or any other position for three months.

items.q: After three months can I apply again?
items.a: Yes, for the same and other positions as per availability of vacant positions.

items.q: Does an unsuccessful IJT affect my current job?
items.a: The policy does not say so. Confidentiality is expected throughout.

items.q: Will I be on probation in my new role?
items.a: Transferred employees may be subject to a 3-month probation period in the new role.

items.q: What is evaluated during probation?
items.a: Your performance and fit for the position.

items.q: What if I do not complete the probation satisfactorily?
items.a: Then he/she would have to leave the organization, as per policy.

items.q: Does this mean my job is at risk if I fail in the new role?
items.a: Yes. The policy says if an employee does not complete the probation period satisfactorily, they would have to leave the organization.

items.q: How long is the notice period for IJT?
items.a: The HOD and HR will decide an appropriate notice period, with a minimum of 45 days.

items.q: Can the notice period be more than 45 days?
items.a: Yes, it may vary based on the complexity of the roles involved.

items.q: Can I join the new role earlier than 45 days?
items.a: The notice period is minimum 45 days. The HOD with HR decides. Early transition is not guaranteed.

items.q: Who decides my notice period?
items.a: The HOD along with HR.

items.q: What happens during the notice period?
items.a: You transition out of your current role to the new one with a plan from your current and new managers.

items.q: Will my salary increase after IJT?
items.a: Not automatically. Benefits remain unchanged, and any compensation adjustment is considered during the appraisal cycle (April) only.

items.q: When will I get a salary change after moving?
items.a: Only at the April appraisal, as per eligibility criteria and the appraisal process.

items.q: Will my existing benefits change?
items.a: No. Employee benefits remain unchanged.

items.q: Who decides compensation adjustments?
items.a: HR and the HOD, in line with the organization's compensation policies.

items.q: Can I negotiate a hike at the time of transfer?
items.a: The policy says compensation adjustments are considered in the April appraisal cycle only.

items.q: Will my leave balance carry over to the new role?
items.a: Benefits remain unchanged, so your leave balance continues.

items.q: I am in Sales and want to move to Support under the same VP. Is it possible?
items.a: Yes, if both are under the same VP and the designation level is the same, after 6 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: I want to move from Support to Marketing under a different VP after 10 months. Can I?
items.a: No. A different VP requires 18 months.

items.q: I was selected but my manager does not want to release me.
items.a: Your current and new managers plan the transition with HR. The HOD and HR decide the notice period (minimum 45 days).

items.q: Can HR transfer me without my application?
items.a: The policy covers employee-initiated IJT. Other transfers depend on company needs.

items.q: Will my appraisal be affected if I move mid-year?
items.a: Any compensation adjustment is considered in the April cycle. Please ask HR for how your performance is evaluated.

items.q: Who do I contact for doubts about IJT?
items.a: The HR department.

items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja can modify or update this policy to meet organizational needs.

items.q: Is the IJT policy applicable to contract employees?
items.a: The policy is for employees meeting the stated criteria. Please check with HR.

items.q: Do I have to give a reason for wanting to transfer?
items.a: Yes. You must specify your reasons for seeking transfer and how your skills align with the new position.

items.q: Can I apply to an opening in another city?
items.a: The policy does not say anything about location. Please check the job posting and ask HR.

items.q: I want to change my department. What should I do?
items.a: Check that you meet the service (6 or 18 months), performance and conduct criteria, wait for an internal opening email, and apply on the Klimb platform with your reasons and skill match.

items.q: Am I eligible for IJT?
items.a: If you have 6 months (same VP) or 18 months (different VP) in your current department and designation, satisfactory performance, and no formal disciplinary action in the last six months, you are eligible.

items.q: How many months do I need for IJT under the same VP?
items.a: 6 months.

items.q: How many months do I need for IJT under a different VP?
items.a: 18 months.

items.q: How long should I wait for the second IJT?
items.a: 18 months in your current department and designation.

items.q: What if my IJT application is rejected?
items.a: You can reapply for the same or other positions only after three months.

items.q: Is IJT compulsory for all department changes?
items.a: Yes, an employee-initiated move to another department goes through the IJT process.

items.q: Can I apply for IJT if I am on a notice period?
items.a: Employees who have resigned are not covered by the policy as an eligible case. Please check with HR.

items.q: What is the Klimb platform?
items.a: It is the platform used to submit IJT applications and to share resumes of referred candidates.

items.q: Can I ask HR to share the feedback on my IJT interview?
items.a: You may ask HR. The policy says all process details are confidential.

items.q: Will I get a new designation in IJT?
items.a: IJT is for the same designation level in a different department.

items.q: Who is the hiring manager in IJT?
items.a: The manager of the department with the open position.

items.q: Do I have to go through interviews even if I am a top performer?
items.a: Yes. All applicants go through screening, assessment and interviews.

items.q: Can I go back if I am not selected in probation?
items.a: The policy says if the probation is not completed satisfactorily, the employee would have to leave the organization.

items.q: Is the 3-month probation always applicable?
items.a: It says "may be subject to" a 3-month probation. HR will confirm for your case.

items.q: Will my current manager's feedback be part of the decision?
items.a: The policy mentions satisfactory performance in the current role as an eligibility condition.

items.q: Is the minimum notice period of 45 days also for IJT within the same VP?
items.a: The policy states a minimum of 45 days upon approval of the transfer. HR and HOD decide.

items.q: Can I apply for IJT in two different departments at the same time?
items.a: The policy does not restrict it. If both are rejected, the three-month waiting period applies.

items.q: Is salary hike part of IJT?
items.a: No. Compensation adjustments are considered only at the April appraisal.

items.q: Which month is the appraisal cycle?
items.a: April.

items.q: Does IJT change my reporting manager?
items.a: Yes, if the new role has a different hiring manager.

items.q: Can the company reject an IJT because of business needs?
items.a: Selection is based on merit and job requirements. Transition is planned by both managers and HR.

items.q: Does a formal disciplinary action from 7 months ago block my IJT?
items.a: No. The restriction applies only to action in the past six months.

items.q: I got my transfer letter. What is my next step?
items.a: Your current and new managers will plan the transition with HR, and you will serve the notice period decided by the HOD and HR (minimum 45 days).

items.q: Will my team know that I applied?
items.a: All persons involved must keep application details confidential.

items.q: Can HR share my application with my current manager?
items.a: Only for the necessary process. Everyone involved must maintain confidentiality.

items.q: Is there any bias protection in selection?
items.a: Yes. The organization is committed to equal opportunity, and selection is on skills, qualifications and performance.

items.q: What if I do not meet the qualifications for the new role?
items.a: You must meet the qualifications and requirements of the desired position to be eligible.

items.q: Does the 6 months count if I was on leave for some time?
items.a: The policy says completion of 6 months in the department and designation. Please ask HR about leave periods.

items.q: What is the Internship Policy?
items.a: It lays down the guidelines, terms and conditions for interns during their internship at Petpooja.

items.q: What topics does the policy cover?
items.a: Internship duration and working conditions, attendance and leave, stipend and statutory compliance, code of conduct and confidentiality, and completion, discontinuation or termination.

items.q: What is the effective date of this policy?
items.a: 08-05-2026 (Draft Version 1.0).

items.q: Does the policy apply to full-time employees?
