items.a: No. It applies to interns.

items.q: Can the company change the internship policy?
items.a: Yes. The company reserves the right to amend internship policies at any time.

items.q: How long is my internship?
items.a: The duration is fixed and mentioned in your Internship Letter/Offer Letter.

items.q: Can my internship be extended?
items.a: Yes. Extension is based on company requirements and management approval.

items.q: Can I ask for an extension?
items.a: You can request, but extension depends on company requirements and management approval.

items.q: Is an extension guaranteed if I perform well?
items.a: No. Extension depends on the company's needs and management approval.

items.q: Will I get a job after the internship?
items.a: The policy does not promise a job offer after the internship.

items.q: Where can I check my internship duration?
items.a: In your Internship Letter or Offer Letter.

items.q: What are my working hours as an intern?
items.a: Interns must follow the company's official working hours.

items.q: Do I need to be punctual?
items.a: Yes. Punctuality and regular attendance are mandatory.

items.q: Who can change my shift timing?
items.a: Any change in working hours or shift timing is communicated by the HR department.

items.q: Can I choose my own timings?
items.a: No. You follow the official working hours, and any change is communicated by HR.

items.q: Do interns work on weekends?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. Follow the working hours communicated by HR.

items.q: How do I mark attendance?
items.a: Interns must mark attendance regularly through the company's attendance system.

items.q: Can I take leave as an intern?
items.a: Yes, with prior approval from your Reporting Manager and HR.

items.q: Whose approval do I need for leave?
items.a: Both your Reporting Manager and HR.

items.q: Can I take leave without approval?
items.a: No. Unauthorized absence may lead to termination of the internship.

items.q: I fell sick suddenly. What should I do?
items.a: Inform your Reporting Manager and HR immediately. Prior approval is required for leave, so seek approval as early as possible.

items.q: What happens if I remain absent continuously?
items.a: Continuous absenteeism may lead to termination of the internship.

items.q: Do interns get paid leave?
items.a: The policy does not mention paid leave. The stipend is subject to attendance and performance.

items.q: How many leaves can I take in a month?
items.a: The policy does not specify a number. Leave needs prior approval from your Reporting Manager and HR.

items.q: Do I get Casual or Sick Leave like full-time employees?
items.a: The Leave Policy applies to full-time employees. For interns, only the Internship Policy rules apply.

items.q: How much stipend will I get?
items.a: As mentioned in your Internship Letter.

items.q: When is the stipend paid?
items.a: It is processed monthly.

items.q: Is the stipend guaranteed every month?
items.a: It is processed monthly, subject to attendance and performance.

items.q: Can my stipend be cut for absence?
items.a: The stipend is subject to attendance, so yes, absences may affect it.

items.q: Will there be tax or other deductions?
items.a: Applicable statutory deductions, if any, will be made as per company policy and government regulations.

items.q: Do I get PF or bonus as an intern?
items.a: The policy only mentions statutory deductions if applicable. It does not mention PF or bonus for interns.

items.q: Can I ask for a stipend hike?
items.a: The stipend is as per your Internship Letter. Any change depends on management.

items.q: Who processes my stipend?
items.a: The company processes it monthly as per the payroll process.

items.q: What behaviour is expected from interns?
items.a: Professional behavior at all times.

items.q: What happens if I violate the code of conduct?
items.a: Misconduct, harassment, discrimination or violation of company policies results in disciplinary action.

items.q: Do interns have to follow company rules?
items.a: Yes. Interns must follow all company rules, security policies and compliance guidelines.

items.q: Does the PoSH policy apply to interns?
items.a: Yes. The PoSH Policy covers interns, trainees and apprentices, and the Internship Policy treats harassment as misconduct.

items.q: Is discrimination allowed?
items.a: No. It leads to disciplinary action.

items.q: What information do I need to keep confidential?
items.a: Company data, processes, clients and internal communications.

items.q: Can I share project details with my friends?
items.a: No. Sharing confidential information with any external person or organization is strictly prohibited.

items.q: Can I post about my work on LinkedIn?
items.a: Do not share confidential information. Check with your manager before posting anything about company work.

items.q: Does confidentiality continue after the internship?
items.a: The policy requires strict confidentiality. Please assume it continues after the internship ends, and check with HR.

items.q: What if I accidentally share confidential data?
items.a: Inform your Reporting Manager and HR immediately. Breach of confidentiality can lead to termination.

items.q: Who monitors my performance?
items.a: Your Reporting Manager.

items.q: Will I get feedback?
items.a: Feedback may be provided periodically during the internship.

items.q: Will I get an internship completion certificate?
items.a: Completion certificates may be issued based on satisfactory performance and conduct.

items.q: Is the certificate guaranteed?
items.a: No. It depends on satisfactory performance and conduct.

items.q: Will I get a certificate if I leave early?
items.a: The policy does not guarantee it. The certificate is based on satisfactory performance and conduct.

items.q: Will I get an experience letter?
items.a: The policy mentions only a completion certificate based on satisfactory performance and conduct.

items.q: Can I use the company laptop for personal work?
items.a: No. Company systems, devices, email IDs and other resources must be used only for official purposes.

items.q: What if I damage a company device?
items.a: Any damage or misuse of company assets may result in recovery or disciplinary action.

items.q: Can I use my company email ID for personal sign-ups?
items.a: No. Company email IDs must be used only for official purposes.

items.q: Will I get a laptop as an intern?
items.a: The policy does not say. Resources are provided as per your team's needs.

items.q: Can the company terminate my internship?
items.a: Yes, in cases such as unsatisfactory performance, misconduct or policy violation, breach of confidentiality, continuous absenteeism or indiscipline, and submission of false information or documents.

items.q: What counts as misconduct?
items.a: Unprofessional behavior, harassment, discrimination, or violation of company policies.

items.q: What if I submit a fake document?
items.a: Submission of false information or documents is a ground for termination.

items.q: Can I be terminated for poor performance?
items.a: Yes. Unsatisfactory performance is a ground for termination.

items.q: Will I get a warning before termination?
items.a: The policy does not mention a warning step. The company has the right to terminate in the listed cases.

items.q: Can I leave my internship early?
items.a: Either party may discontinue the internship by giving prior notice as per company policy.

items.q: How long is the notice period for an intern?
items.a: The policy says as per company policy. Please check with HR for the exact days.

items.q: Can the company waive my notice period?
items.a: Yes. The company may waive the notice period depending on the situation.

items.q: Can the company end my internship without notice?
items.a: The company may terminate in the listed cases, and may waive the notice period depending on the situation.

items.q: I got a full-time job offer elsewhere. Can I leave?
items.a: Yes, by giving prior notice as per company policy.

items.q: Who communicates changes in the policy?
items.a: The HR department communicates instructions and changes from time to time.

items.q: Do I need to follow HR policies?
items.a: Yes. All interns must comply with company HR policies and instructions communicated from time to time.

items.q: What kind of ethical conduct is expected?
items.a: Professionalism, discipline and ethical conduct.

items.q: Whom do I approach for any issue during the internship?
items.a: Your Reporting Manager and HR.

items.q: Is the internship a job guarantee?
items.a: No. The policy does not provide for a guaranteed job.

items.q: Can an intern refer a candidate?
items.a: The Referral Policy applies to regular employees only. Interns are not mentioned.

items.q: Can an intern take a company loan?
items.a: No. The Loan Policy is for confirmed full-time employees with 2 years of service.

items.q: Can an intern apply for a salary advance?
items.a: No. Salary advance is for confirmed full-time employees with at least six months of service.

items.q: Does the Leave Policy apply to interns?
items.a: No. It applies to full-time employees on regular payroll.

items.q: Is the internship duration changeable?
items.a: It is fixed as per your offer letter, and changes depend on management approval.

items.q: I am a new intern. What should I do on my first day?
items.a: Follow the company's working hours, mark attendance in the attendance system, and read your Internship Letter and this policy.

items.q: Where is my stipend amount mentioned?
items.a: In your Internship Letter/Offer Letter.

items.q: Is the stipend paid even if I do not perform well?
items.a: The stipend is processed monthly, subject to attendance and performance.

items.q: What if my attendance is low in a month?
items.a: Your stipend may be affected, since it is subject to attendance and performance. Continuous absenteeism can also lead to termination.

items.q: Do I need to inform HR about leave, or only my manager?
items.a: Both. Prior approval from your Reporting Manager and HR is required.

items.q: Can I work from home as an intern?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. Follow the official working hours and any arrangement communicated by HR.

items.q: Do I get public holidays?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. Please confirm with HR.

items.q: Can I get a letter of recommendation?
items.a: The policy mentions only a completion certificate based on satisfactory performance and conduct.

items.q: Can I intern with another company at the same time?
items.a: The policy requires interns to follow all company rules and maintain confidentiality. Please check with HR before taking another assignment.

items.q: What if I want to extend my internship?
items.a: Talk to your Reporting Manager. Extension depends on company requirements and management approval.

items.q: Who decides my extension?
items.a: Management.

items.q: Who gives me feedback during the internship?
items.a: Your Reporting Manager monitors performance and may give periodic feedback.

items.q: Will interns go through PoSH awareness?
items.a: The PoSH Policy covers interns, trainees and apprentices, so every intern is protected and expected to follow it.

items.q: Can I file a harassment complaint as an intern?
items.a: Yes. You can file a complaint with the Internal Committee (ICC) under the PoSH Policy.

items.q: Is discrimination against interns allowed?
items.a: No. Discrimination is misconduct and leads to disciplinary action.

items.q: Can I use company software for my college project?
items.a: No. Company resources must be used only for official purposes.

items.q: Can I take company data for my college report?
items.a: No. Sharing company data, processes or clients externally is strictly prohibited.

items.q: What happens if I lose the company laptop?
items.a: Any damage or misuse of company assets may result in recovery or disciplinary action.

items.q: Can the company terminate me for indiscipline?
items.a: Yes. Continuous absenteeism or indiscipline is a ground for termination.

items.q: Do I need to follow the security policies of the company?
items.a: Yes. Interns must follow all company rules, security policies and compliance guidelines.

items.q: Will I be paid for the notice period?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. Please check with HR.

items.q: How do I formally end my internship early?
items.a: Give prior notice as per company policy to your Reporting Manager and HR.

items.q: Can the company ask me to leave immediately?
items.a: In the listed cases, the company may terminate and may waive the notice period depending on the situation.

items.q: Will I be given an offer for full-time work?
items.a: The policy does not provide for it. Performance and company needs decide.

items.q: Is the policy a draft?
items.a: It is marked Draft Version 1.0 with effective date 08-05-2026.

items.q: What if my reporting manager changes?
items.a: The new Reporting Manager monitors your performance. Inform HR if you have concerns.

items.q: Can the HR change my shift?
items.a: Yes. HR communicates any change in working hours or shift timing.

items.q: Can I submit my own documents like ID proof later?
items.a: Submit all required documents on time. False information or documents can lead to termination.

items.q: Whom should I contact for anything not covered in the policy?
items.a: HR and your Reporting Manager.

items.q: Who is covered under the Leave Policy?
items.a: All full-time employees on the regular payroll of Prayosha Food Services Private Limited (Petpooja).

items.q: Does the Leave Policy apply to interns?
items.a: No. It applies only to full-time employees on regular payroll.

items.q: What is the leave year?
items.a: The calendar year (January to December).

items.q: How is leave credited to me?
items.a: Leave is automatically allotted in the HRMS software.

items.q: Is leave approval guaranteed?
items.a: No. Sanctioning of leave is at management's discretion based on business exigencies or the seriousness of the case.

items.q: What types of leave do I get?
items.a: Privilege Leave (PL), Casual Leave (CL), Sick Leave (SL), Maternity Leave, Probationary Leave (PBL), Paternity Leave, Wedding Leave, Public Holidays and Leave Without Pay (LWP).

items.q: How many public holidays do I get?
items.a: 13 in a year: 10 fixed holidays and 3 optional holidays.

items.q: When is the public holiday list announced?
items.a: At the beginning of the year.

items.q: Are public holidays carried forward or encashed?
items.a: No.

items.q: Which leaves can I carry forward to the next year?
items.a: Privilege Leave (up to 63) and Sick Leave (up to 14). Casual Leave does not carry forward.

items.q: Which leaves can be encashed?
items.a: Only Privilege Leave, at the time of relieving.

items.q: What is the minimum I can apply for in one request?
items.a: PL: 2 days. CL, SL, PBL, Paternity and Wedding Leave: 1/2 day.

items.q: How do I check my leave balance?
items.a: In the HRMS portal, or with the HR department.

items.q: How do I apply for leave?
items.a: Through the HRMS portal. Your reporting manager can approve or reject it on valid grounds.

items.q: Who approves my leave?
items.a: Your reporting manager.

items.q: How many Privilege Leaves do I get?
items.a: A maximum of 15 days in a calendar year.

items.q: When do I become eligible for PL?
items.a: After completing 240 pay days from your date of joining.

items.q: What are "pay days"?
items.a: The days for which you are paid salary. Days on LOP are not counted.

items.q: How is PL credited to new joiners?
items.a: Once you complete 240 pay days, a maximum of 10 leaves are credited on a pro-rata basis as per your pay days. After that, you accrue 1.25 days every month on a pro-rata basis.

items.q: How is PL credited to regular employees?
items.a: 1.25 days every month on a pro-rata basis depending on your pay days in that month, up to 15 days a year.

items.q: Will LOP days reduce my PL?
items.a: Yes. PL credit depends on pay days, and LOP days are not counted for PL eligibility.

items.q: How early should I apply for planned PL?
items.a: At least 15 days before, and it should be approved by your reporting authority before you go on leave.

items.q: I need PL urgently for an emergency. What should I do?
items.a: Inform your reporting manager and HR on the same day through email.

items.q: What if I take PL without approval?
items.a: Any unapproved leave is treated as leave without pay.

items.q: What is the minimum PL I can take?
items.a: 2 days.

items.q: Can I take PL for a single day?
items.a: The minimum PL per request is 2 days. For a single day, use CL or SL as applicable.

items.q: Can I carry forward unused PL?
items.a: Yes. Unused PL is carried forward, with a cap of 63 leaves for encashment purposes.

items.q: What happens to PL above 63 days?
items.a: Any PL above 63 days lapses automatically and is not eligible for encashment.

items.q: Can I encash my PL while working?
items.a: No. PL encashment is done at the time of relieving, along with Full and Final settlement.

items.q: On what salary is PL encashed?
items.a: On your last drawn Basic Salary.

items.q: I have 40 PL and I am resigning. What happens?
items.a: You get encashment for the PL balance at your last drawn basic salary in your Full and Final settlement, as per company process.

items.q: Can PL balance be used to adjust my unserved notice period?
items.a: Yes. The amount payable for unserved notice can be adjusted against the amount payable for balance PL, as per the Separation Policy.

items.q: I joined 5 months ago. Can I take PL?
items.a: No. You become eligible after 240 pay days.

items.q: Will I get PL during probation?
items.a: Only once you complete 240 pay days. During probation, you have Probationary Leave (PBL).

items.q: How many Casual Leaves do I get?
items.a: 7 days in a calendar year.

items.q: Who is eligible for CL?
items.a: All full-time confirmed employees.

items.q: I am on probation. Do I get CL?
items.a: No. CL is added once you complete probation and are confirmed.

items.q: Will CL be pro-rated if I join mid-year?
items.a: Yes. CL is pro-rated for employees appointed during the year.

items.q: Can I carry forward my CL?
items.a: No. Unused CL lapses on December 31st.

items.q: Can I encash my CL?
items.a: No.

items.q: How many CLs can I take at a stretch?
items.a: Not more than 3 days at a stretch.

items.q: How early should I apply for CL?
items.a: At least 2 days before, with approval from your reporting authority.

items.q: What should I do in an emergency when I cannot apply 2 days earlier?
items.a: Inform your reporting manager and HR on the same day through phone or email.

items.q: What if I don't get my CL approved but I take the leave?
items.a: It will be treated as leave without pay.

items.q: Can I take half-day CL?
items.a: Yes. The minimum is 1/2 day.

items.q: Can I take 5 CL in a row?
items.a: No. The maximum is 3 days at a stretch.

items.q: How many Sick Leaves do I get?
items.a: 7 days in a calendar year.

items.q: Who is eligible for SL?
items.a: All full-time confirmed employees.

items.q: Can I carry forward my SL?
items.a: Yes, up to 14 days. Balance above 14 lapses.

items.q: Can I encash SL?
items.a: No.

items.q: Is SL pro-rated for new joiners?
items.a: Yes, for employees appointed during the year.

items.q: Do I need a medical certificate for SL?
items.a: Yes, for SL taken beyond 2 days you must submit medical documents or a doctor's prescription.

items.q: I took 2 days sick leave. Do I need a medical certificate?
items.a: No. A certificate is needed if more than 2 days are taken under SL.

items.q: I took 3 days SL. What do I do?
items.a: Submit medical documents or a doctor's prescription.

items.q: When should I update SL in HRMS?
items.a: Within 3 days of joining back in the office.

items.q: Till when do SLs need to be approved?
items.a: By the end of the month on HRMS.

items.q: Can I take half-day SL?
items.a: Yes. The minimum is 1/2 day.

items.q: I am sick but my SL is finished. What can I do?
items.a: You can use other available leave such as PL or CL (if eligible). If none is available, it will be LWP.

items.q: What leave do I get during probation?
items.a: 5 Probationary Leaves (PBL).

items.q: Does PBL apply in extended probation?
items.a: Yes. The total is 5 PBL for the probation or extended probation period.

items.q: What if I take more than 5 days during probation?
items.a: The rest will be LWP (leave without pay).

items.q: What happens to unused PBL after I get confirmed?
items.a: It lapses.

items.q: Can I take leave during product training?
items.a: Leave taken during the product training period is treated as leave without pay.

items.q: Can I take half-day PBL?
items.a: Yes. The minimum is 1/2 day.

items.q: Do I get CL or SL during probation?
items.a: No. CL and SL are credited after you complete probation and get confirmed.

items.q: Who is eligible for Maternity Leave?
items.a: A woman who has worked in the establishment for at least 80 days in the past 12 months, as per the law.

items.q: How many days of Maternity Leave do I get?
items.a: 26 weeks (182 days) of paid leave.

items.q: Can I take leave before the delivery?
items.a: Yes. You can adjust the leave before and after the delivery, totaling 182 days.

items.q: What should I submit before availing ML?
items.a: A certificate from a gynecologist mentioning the expected date of delivery.

items.q: How early should I apply?
items.a: By email to your manager at least 8 weeks before your expected confinement, with a medical certificate.

items.q: Are weekly offs and holidays inside ML counted?
items.a: Yes. Intervening national, declared and festival holidays and weekly offs are counted as part of the leave.

items.q: What if my leave needs to be extended due to complications?
items.a: It can be extended, but it will fall under LOP if no casual leaves are available.

items.q: Can ML exceed 26 weeks?
items.a: No. Maternity leave shall not exceed 26 weeks.

items.q: What leave do I get in case of a miscarriage?
items.a: Up to 42 days, with a medical certificate from a registered gynecologist.

items.q: What if the pregnancy is terminated without medical advice?
items.a: If it is terminated without the advice of a registered gynecologist or without any genuine reason, no leave is granted.

items.q: What leave do I get for surrogacy?
items.a: 12 weeks of leave for "Commissioning Mothers".

items.q: How do I apply for commissioning leave?
items.a: By email to the HR team with the required details.

items.q: What leave do I get for adoption?
items.a: A woman who legally adopts a child below three months gets maternity benefit for 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over.

items.q: Can I work somewhere else during maternity leave?
items.a: No. A woman employee may not work at any other establishment during her maternity leave.

items.q: Do I have to go to site visits during my pregnancy?
items.a: Female employees are excused from site visits from 10 weeks before the due date.

items.q: Am I expected to work in the last weeks before delivery?
items.a: The company does not expect you to work from 4 weeks before the due date. Working beyond that is voluntary and at your own risk.

items.q: Do I get nursing breaks after I return?
items.a: Yes. You get two nursing breaks of prescribed duration in your daily work until the child is fifteen months old, in addition to the rest interval.

items.q: Is Maternity Leave paid?
items.a: Yes. 26 weeks of paid leave as per the law.

items.q: How many days of paternity leave do I get?
items.a: Up to 5 days.

items.q: Who is eligible?
items.a: All male full-time confirmed employees.

items.q: Within what time must I take paternity leave?
items.a: Within one month of your spouse's delivery.

items.q: How many times can I take paternity leave?
items.a: Maximum 2 occasions during your tenure.

items.q: What do I need to submit?
items.a: A certificate issued by a Registered Medical Practitioner indicating the date of delivery.

items.q: What if I do not take it within the month?
items.a: It lapses.

items.q: Can I take half-day paternity leave?
items.a: Yes. The minimum is 1/2 day.

items.q: How many days of Wedding Leave do I get?
items.a: Up to 10 days of paid leave.

items.q: Who is eligible?
items.a: All full-time confirmed employees.

items.q: How many times can I avail Wedding Leave?
items.a: Once during your tenure with Petpooja.

items.q: What do I need to submit?
items.a: A copy of your wedding invitation card to HR before your leave starts, along with your manager's approval confirmation.

items.q: What if I do not take it in the period?
items.a: It lapses.

items.q: Can I take Wedding Leave for my brother's or sister's wedding?
items.a: No. Wedding Leave is for your own wedding.

items.q: Can I take Wedding Leave during probation?
items.a: No. It is for confirmed employees.

items.q: Can I take half-day Wedding Leave?
items.a: Yes. The minimum is 1/2 day.

items.q: When is LOP applied?
items.a: When no other leave is available, or the leave is taken without prior approval.

items.q: Do I get any pay during LOP?
items.a: No. You are not entitled to any pay or allowance during LOP.

items.q: How long can I take LOP?
items.a: A maximum of 3 months with management approval (for exceptional cases like ML/SL).

items.q: What if I do not return after sanctioned LOP?
items.a: It is considered that you have abandoned your service on your own accord.

items.q: Can the company apply LOP as a disciplinary action?
items.a: Yes. LOP can be applied on disciplinary grounds for attendance issues, regardless of other leave availability.

items.q: I took LOP on Friday and Monday. What happens to Saturday and Sunday?
items.a: The weekly offs in between are also counted as LOP.

items.q: Does LOP before or after a holiday affect the holiday?
items.a: Yes. The holiday or weekly off is also counted as LOP.

items.q: Do LOP days count for PL eligibility?
items.a: No. LOP days are not counted for PL eligibility.

items.q: Can my approved leave be cancelled?
items.a: Yes. The Department Head can cancel sanctioned leave on a situational or need basis.

items.q: What if I go on leave that has been cancelled?
items.a: Those days are treated as absence from duty.

items.q: Can I extend my leave?
items.a: Yes, with prior approval from your Department Head, applied well in advance.

items.q: What if I overstay my leave?
items.a: Unsanctioned leave days are treated as absence from duty.

items.q: What is absence from duty?
items.a: Taking days off without prior approval or proper intimation. These days are treated as Loss of Pay.

items.q: What should I do when I return from absence?
items.a: Report to your Department Head and give valid reasons for the absence in writing before resuming work.

items.q: What if I am absent for more than 7 days continuously?
items.a: HR sends an official letter asking you to report to duty and explain. Holidays and weekly offs in between are included.

items.q: What if I do not reply to the HR letter?
items.a: If there is no response within the stipulated time, it is assumed that you have withdrawn your service on your own accord.

items.q: Who decides action in case of long absence?
items.a: Management decides based on the enquiry.

items.q: Can leave be approved retroactively?
items.a: Leave should be approved before. Unapproved leave is treated as LWP, but in emergencies you must inform the manager and HR on the same day.

items.q: Does my manager's no-action on my leave matter?
items.a: Under the Attendance Policy, if the manager takes no action on leave, the manager's LWP is considered. Follow up with your manager and HR.

items.q: Am I eligible for a loan?
items.a: If you are a confirmed full-time employee and have completed two years with the company, and you are in good standing, you are eligible for the company's employee loan.

items.q: I want a loan.
items.a: If you have completed two years in Petpooja as a confirmed full-time employee and are in good standing, you can apply for a loan for a genuine financial need listed in the policy. Take written approval from your manager and send it to HR.

items.q: I joined 1 year 6 months ago. Can I get a loan?
items.a: No. You must complete two years of active employment.

items.q: I completed exactly 2 years yesterday. Can I apply?
items.a: Yes, provided you are a confirmed full-time employee in good standing.

items.q: I have 2 years of service but I am still on probation. Can I apply?
items.a: No. Only confirmed full-time employees are eligible.

items.q: What does "good standing" mean?
items.a: You should have no serious disciplinary, conduct or attendance issues with the company.

items.q: Is the loan for any purpose?
items.a: No. It is available in the event of a personal financial crisis for the purposes listed in the policy.

items.q: Can a part-time employee, contract employee or intern take a loan?
items.a: No. Only confirmed full-time employees with two years of active service.

items.q: Is the loan interest-free?
items.a: Yes. The policy does not charge any interest on the loan. You repay only the loan amount in equal EMIs through payroll deductions.

items.q: Is the loan a right?
items.a: No. It is at the company's discretion to approve or not approve any loan request. The company may deny a loan for any reason.

items.q: I am eligible. How much loan can I get?
items.a: With 2 years of service: up to 2 times your monthly gross salary (8 equal EMIs). With 5 years: up to 3 times your monthly gross salary (12 equal EMIs). With more than 7 years: up to 5 times your monthly gross salary (18 equal EMIs).

items.q: I have completed 2 years. How much can I get?
items.a: Up to 2 times your monthly gross salary, repayable in 8 equal EMIs.

items.q: I have completed 5 years. How much can I get?
items.a: Up to 3 times your monthly gross salary, repayable in 12 equal EMIs.

items.q: I have completed more than 7 years. How much can I get?
items.a: Up to 5 times your monthly gross salary, repayable in 18 equal EMIs.

items.q: I have 3 years of service. Which slab applies to me?
items.a: The 2-year slab (up to 2 times gross, 8 EMIs), since you have not yet completed 5 years.

items.q: I have 6 years of service. Which slab applies to me?
items.a: The 5-year slab (up to 3 times gross, 12 EMIs), since you have not yet completed more than 7 years.

items.q: I have exactly 7 years of service. Which slab applies?
items.a: The policy says "more than 7 years" for the 5 times slab. At exactly 7 years the 3-times slab applies. Please confirm with HR.

items.q: My monthly gross salary is Rs. 50,000 with 2 years of service. What is my maximum loan?
items.a: Rs. 1,00,000 (2 x 50,000), repayable in 8 EMIs of Rs. 12,500.

items.q: My monthly gross salary is Rs. 60,000 with 5 years of service. What is my maximum loan?
items.a: Rs. 1,80,000 (3 x 60,000), repayable in 12 EMIs of Rs. 15,000.

items.q: My monthly gross salary is Rs. 80,000 with more than 7 years of service. What is my maximum loan?
items.a: Rs. 4,00,000 (5 x 80,000), repayable in 18 EMIs of about Rs. 22,222.

items.q: Is the loan calculated on net salary or gross?
items.a: On monthly gross salary.

items.q: Can I take less than the maximum?
items.a: Yes. The loan amount must not exceed your eligibility. You can apply for a smaller amount.

items.q: Can I get more than my eligibility if my need is big?
items.a: No. The amount of the loan must not exceed your eligibility.

items.q: Who decides the exact amount sanctioned?
items.a: The CFO and HR review the application, considering the purpose, the amount, and your outstanding indebtedness.

items.q: For what reasons can I take a company loan?
items.a: Medical emergency of first family not covered by insurance, natural disasters, death in the first family, abroad education expenses of siblings and children, your or your sibling's marriage, purchase or repair of an official laptop, and purchase of a mobile handset.

items.q: Can I take a loan for a medical emergency?
items.a: Yes, for a medical emergency of your first family that is not covered by any medical insurance policy.

items.q: What is "first family"?
items.a: Your immediate family. Please check with HR for the exact definition.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my own wedding?
items.a: Yes. Self or siblings marriage expenses are an eligible purpose.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my sister's wedding?
items.a: Yes. Siblings marriage expenses are an eligible purpose.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my child's wedding?
items.a: The policy lists self or siblings marriage only. Please check with HR for other cases.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my child's school fees?
items.a: The policy mentions abroad education or study expenses of siblings and children. Other education expenses are not listed.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my child's education abroad?
items.a: Yes. Abroad education expenses of siblings and children are an eligible purpose.

items.q: Can I take a loan for a death in my family?
items.a: Yes. Sudden bereavement or funeral expenses for immediate family members are covered.

items.q: Can I take a loan after a natural disaster?
items.a: Yes. Loss of property or livelihood due to events like earthquakes or floods is covered.

items.q: Can I take a loan to buy a laptop?
items.a: Yes, for a new laptop for official use.

items.q: Can I take a loan to repair my laptop?
items.a: Yes, for repair of a laptop used for official work.

items.q: Can I take a loan to buy a mobile phone?
items.a: Yes. Rs. 30,000 or your eligibility amount, whichever is lower, is approved. This is allowed once every 3 years and invoice submission is mandatory.

items.q: Can I get a mobile loan of Rs. 50,000?
items.a: No. The maximum for a mobile handset is Rs. 30,000 or your eligibility amount, whichever is lower.

items.q: Can I take a mobile loan every year?
items.a: No. It is allowed once every 3 years.

items.q: Do I need to submit the mobile invoice?
items.a: Yes. Invoice submission is mandatory.

items.q: Can I take a loan for buying a house or vehicle?
items.a: No. These purposes are not listed in the policy.

items.q: Can I take a loan to repay my other debts?
items.a: No. This is not a listed purpose.

items.q: Can I take a loan for a vacation?
items.a: No. The loan is for unexpected financial crises or listed purposes.

items.q: What is an "unexpected financial crisis"?
items.a: An unplanned expense, such as medical emergency, natural disaster loss or a death in the first family.

items.q: Is the list of purposes complete?
items.a: The policy says "such as, but not limited to" for crisis examples. HR and the CFO decide on genuine cases.

items.q: Do I need to give proof of the purpose?
items.a: Please be ready with supporting documents. The mobile purchase explicitly needs an invoice.

items.q: How do I apply for a loan?
items.a: Get written approval from your immediate manager, who signs and forwards the request to HR at hr@petpooja.com.

items.q: Who reviews my loan application?
items.a: The CFO and HR.

items.q: What criteria are used to prioritize applications?
items.a: Purpose of the loan, amount of the loan (not exceeding eligibility), and your outstanding indebtedness.

items.q: Will I be informed about approval or rejection?
items.a: Yes. A member of the HR department will notify you.

items.q: My manager did not approve. Can I still apply?
items.a: No. Written approval from your immediate manager is required.

items.q: What happens if my application is rejected?
items.a: The application is discarded and will not be used for any additional requests. You will need to submit a fresh request if you wish.

items.q: Can I apply again after rejection?
items.a: You can submit a new application. Rejected applications are discarded and not reused.

items.q: Is the approval timeline mentioned?
items.a: The policy mentions payment within 7 working days after approval and submission of relevant documents. The review time is not specified.

items.q: Can the company reject my loan even if I am eligible?
items.a: Yes. The company can deny approval of a loan for any reason.

items.q: What do I need to sign before getting the loan?
items.a: A loan agreement.

items.q: Do I need to give a cheque?
items.a: Yes. You need to submit a cheque at the time of signing the agreement.

items.q: What should be written on the cheque?
items.a: A note saying "Not more than Rs. (Loan Amount)".

items.q: When will I get my cheque back?
items.a: After the loan period is completed.

items.q: When will I get the money?
items.a: Payment is processed by the accounts team within a regular payment cycle of 7 working days after approval and submission of relevant documents.

items.q: Is tax payable on the loan?
items.a: Any tax liability applicable on the loan amount is borne by the employee.

items.q: Who pays the perquisite tax?
items.a: The employee. All taxes as per government law, including perquisite tax if applicable, are borne by the employee.

items.q: Can I transfer my loan benefit to someone else?
items.a: No. The loan program is a personal benefit and is not assignable to any other person.

items.q: How will I repay the loan?
items.a: Through monthly payroll deductions in equal installments, without any lapse or relaxation.

items.q: Can I skip an EMI?
items.a: No. The deductions are made without lapse or relaxation.

items.q: Can I get an EMI holiday in a difficult month?
items.a: No. The policy says no lapse or relaxation.

items.q: How many EMIs will I have for a 2 months' gross salary loan?
items.a: 8 equal EMIs.

items.q: How many EMIs will I have for a 3 months' gross salary loan?
items.a: 12 equal EMIs.

items.q: How many EMIs will I have for a 5 months' gross salary loan?
items.a: 18 equal EMIs.

items.q: Can I repay the loan earlier?
items.a: Yes. You can close the loan by paying the entire outstanding at any time during the repayment period.

items.q: Can I pay part of the outstanding earlier?
items.a: The policy mentions closing the loan by paying the entire outstanding. Please check with HR for part-payments.

items.q: What happens if I resign while the loan is running?
items.a: The entire outstanding becomes due immediately.

items.q: What happens if I am terminated with an unpaid loan?
items.a: The entire outstanding becomes due immediately when you leave the organization.

items.q: Will my relieving letter be issued if I have loan dues?
items.a: No. Relieving letter and clearance formalities will not be completed until all dues are cleared.

items.q: Can the company recover legal costs?
items.a: Yes. The company has the right to recover any legal costs spent in recovering the amount from the employee.

items.q: Will the outstanding loan be adjusted in my Full and Final settlement?
items.a: Yes, dues are settled before separation as per the Separation Policy.

items.q: What if I go on LOP while my loan is running?
items.a: The policy requires repayment through payroll deductions without lapse. Please consult HR on how LOP months are handled.

items.q: Can I take a second loan while the first is running?
items.a: No. You can apply for another loan only when you have a zero balance on prior loans.

items.q: How soon can I take another loan after closing the first?
items.a: There must be a minimum gap of one year.

items.q: I closed my loan last month. Can I apply again?
items.a: No. A gap of at least one year is required.

items.q: Can I take a salary advance while I have a loan?
items.a: No. You are not eligible for a salary advance until your loan is over.

items.q: Does a mobile loan count as a loan for the gap rule?
items.a: Yes. It is also a loan, and the zero-balance and one-year gap rules apply.

items.q: What if I give wrong information in my loan application?
items.a: Misrepresentation or abuse is a cause for discipline, up to and including termination.

items.q: Can the company stop the loan program?
items.a: Yes. The program may be terminated at any time and the company can revise or modify clauses depending on business demand.

items.q: What is the effective date of this policy?
items.a: 01-01-2026 (Draft Version 1.5).

items.q: Who do I contact for loan queries?
items.a: HR, at hr@petpooja.com.

items.q: How much loan can I take?
items.a: It depends on your service: 2 years gives up to 2 times monthly gross salary, 5 years gives up to 3 times, and more than 7 years gives up to 5 times.

items.q: What is the minimum service needed for a loan?
items.a: Two years of active employment as a confirmed full-time employee.

items.q: In how many EMIs will I repay if I take the maximum at 2 years?
items.a: 8 equal EMIs.

items.q: In how many EMIs will I repay if I take the maximum at 5 years?
items.a: 12 equal EMIs.

items.q: In how many EMIs will I repay if I take the maximum at more than 7 years?
items.a: 18 equal EMIs.

items.q: Can I choose my own number of EMIs?
items.a: No. EMIs are fixed by the loan amount slab: 8, 12 or 18.

items.q: If I take only 1 month's gross salary, how many EMIs?
items.a: The policy lists EMIs for 2, 3 and 5 months' gross salary. For smaller amounts, please check with HR.

items.q: What happens to my cheque if I repay the loan early?
items.a: The cheque is returned once the loan period is completed or the loan is closed.

items.q: Can the company deposit my cheque?
items.a: The cheque is submitted as security with the note "Not more than Rs. (Loan Amount)". It is returned after the loan period is completed.

items.q: Can I take a loan for medical expenses covered by insurance?
items.a: No. The medical emergency must not be covered by any medical insurance policy.

items.q: Can I take a loan for my parents' medical treatment?
items.a: Yes, if they are part of your first family and the expense is not covered by insurance.

items.q: My manager is on leave. How do I get approval?
items.a: Get written approval from your immediate manager. Inform HR if your manager is unavailable for long.

items.q: How soon will I get the money after approval?
items.a: Within the regular payment cycle of 7 working days after approval and submission of relevant documents.

items.q: Does the loan affect my in-hand salary?
items.a: Yes. The monthly EMI is deducted from your salary through payroll.

items.q: Can I take another loan after a one-year gap, even if I repaid in full early?
items.a: Yes, after the balance is zero and there is a minimum gap of one year.

items.q: Is the loan available for contract-to-permanent employees?
items.a: Only confirmed full-time employees are eligible. The two years are counted as active employment.

items.q: What if I have already taken a loan from a bank? Will it matter?
items.a: Yes. Your outstanding indebtedness is one of the criteria for prioritizing applications.

items.q: Can I be refused if I have many other loans?
items.a: Yes. Outstanding indebtedness is considered, and the company may deny a loan for any reason.

items.q: What is the No Relative Hiring Policy?
items.a: A policy to keep recruitment and employment fair and unbiased by preventing conflict of interest, favoritism and confidentiality risks that can arise from hiring close relatives of current employees.

items.q: Why does the company have this policy?
items.a: To avoid conflicts of interest, lack of objectivity, damage to team dynamics, risk of confidentiality breach and potential legal issues.

items.q: Who is a "relative" under this policy?
items.a: Any person related by blood, marriage or domestic partnership.

items.q: Who is a "current employee"?
items.a: An individual currently employed by the company.

items.q: What are Family - A and Family - B?
items.a: They are two lists of relatives in Annexure-A. Family - A relatives cannot be hired. Family - B relatives can be hired with conditions.

items.q: Where can I see the list of relatives?
items.a: In Annexure-A of the policy.

items.q: Who tells employees about this policy?
items.a: All employees are informed about it during onboarding.

items.q: Who ensures the policy is applied during hiring?
items.a: HR.

items.q: What happens if the policy is violated?
items.a: Disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment for the involved parties.

items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja can modify, update or revoke the policy without any notification.

items.q: Can I refer my brother for a job in the company?
items.a: No. Brother is in Family - A, and Family - A relatives may not be hired for any position in the company.

items.q: Can my cousin be hired?
items.a: Yes, if the cousin is in Family - B, but only in a different Sr. Authority (reporting line) and a different department.

items.q: What does "different Sr. Authority with different department" mean?
items.a: The Family - B relative must not work under the same senior authority and must be in a different department from the current employee.

items.q: Can a Family - B relative work in my department?
items.a: No. They must be in a different department.

items.q: Can a Family - B relative report to my manager?
items.a: No. They must be under a different senior authority.

items.q: My wife applied for a job here. Can she be hired?
items.a: No. Spouse is in Family - A and cannot be hired.

items.q: Can my husband work in the same company?
items.a: A spouse cannot be hired by the company if you are already an employee. If two employees get married later, see the marriage rule.

items.q: Can my father or mother be hired?
items.a: No. Father and mother are Family - A.

items.q: Can my son or daughter be hired?
items.a: No. Son and daughter are Family - A.

items.q: Can my sister be hired?
items.a: No. Sister (including step sister) is Family - A.

items.q: Can my step brother be hired?
items.a: No. Brother, including step brother, is Family - A.

items.q: Can my step son be hired?
items.a: No. Son, including step son, is Family - A.

items.q: Can my uncle be hired?
items.a: Father's brother, father's sister, mother's brother and mother's sister are Family - A, so they cannot be hired.

items.q: Can my aunt (father's brother's wife) be hired?
items.a: Father's brother's wife is Family - B. She can be hired in a different department and under a different senior authority.

items.q: Can my father-in-law or mother-in-law be hired?
items.a: No. Husband's father and mother, and wife's father and mother, are Family - A.

items.q: Can my brother-in-law or sister-in-law be hired?
items.a: It depends on the relationship. Wife's brother, wife's sister, husband's brother and husband's sister are Family - A. Husband's brother's wife, husband's sister's husband, wife's sister's husband and wife's brother's wife are Family - B.

items.q: Can my daughter-in-law be hired?
items.a: No. Son's wife is Family - A.

items.q: Can my son-in-law be hired?
items.a: No. Daughter's husband is Family - A.

items.q: Can my grandson or granddaughter be hired?
items.a: Son's son, son's daughter, daughter's son and daughter's daughter are Family - A, so they cannot be hired.

items.q: Can my nephew or niece be hired?
items.a: Brother's son and daughter, and sister's son and daughter, are Family - A, so they cannot be hired.

items.q: Can my nephew's wife be hired?
items.a: Brother's son's wife and sister's son's wife are Family - B. She can be hired with the conditions.

items.q: Can my niece's husband be hired?
items.a: Brother's daughter's husband and sister's daughter's husband are Family - B.

items.q: Can my cousin brother or sister be hired?
items.a: Yes, if they fall under Family - B, in a different department and under a different senior authority.

items.q: Which cousins are in Family - B?
items.a: Father's brother's son and daughter, father's sister's son and daughter, mother's sister's son and daughter, and mother's brother's son and daughter.

items.q: Can my boyfriend or girlfriend (significant other) be hired?
items.a: The policy statement includes significant others as close relatives and defines a relative as related by blood, marriage or domestic partnership. Please check with HR.

items.q: Can my domestic partner be hired?
items.a: Relative includes a domestic partnership. A spouse is Family - A. Please check with HR for domestic partners.

items.q: Can my friend be hired?
items.a: Yes. The policy applies to relatives only.

items.q: Can my neighbour's son be hired?
items.a: Yes. He is not a relative.

items.q: I want to refer a relative through the Referral Policy. Is it allowed?
items.a: No. Under the Referral Policy the referred candidate should not be a relative. The No Relative Hiring Policy also applies.

items.a: Father, mother, spouse, brother, sister, daughter, son, father's brother, father's sister, mother's brother, mother's sister, husband's father and mother, husband's brother and sister, wife's father and mother, wife's brother and sister, and others as listed in Annexure-A.

items.a: Yes. Husband's father and mother, and wife's father and mother, are Family - A.

items.a: Yes. Sister's husband is in Family - A.

items.q: Can any Family - A relative work in a different department?
items.a: No. Family - A relatives may not be hired for any position within the company.

items.q: Which relatives are in Family - B?
items.a: Father's brother's wife and children, father's sister's husband and children, mother's sister's children, mother's brother's children, husband's brother's wife, husband's sister's husband, wife's sister's husband, wife's brother's wife, and grandchildren's and nephews'/nieces' spouses, as listed in Annexure-A.

items.a: Yes, with conditions of a different department and a different senior authority.

items.q: If my Family - B relative joins, can they later move to my department?
items.a: No. Any changes in roles or reassignments must follow the policy, which requires a different department and senior authority.

items.q: Two employees of the company get married. What happens?
items.a: One of the individuals is required to transition out of the organization within one month.

items.q: Can both of us continue working after marriage?
items.a: No. As per the policy, one of the two must leave the organization within a period of one month.

items.q: Who decides which of us will leave?
items.a: The policy says one of the individuals involved will be required to transition out. The decision is taken with HR and management.

items.q: Does the same rule apply to domestic partnership?
items.a: Yes. The policy applies on marriage or partnership between two employees.

items.q: Is there a time limit?
items.a: Yes. One month.

items.q: Does this apply to employees already married to each other when the policy came into effect?
items.a: The policy is effective immediately. Please check with HR for existing cases.

items.q: What if we are in different departments?
items.a: The policy says one of the individuals will be required to transition out within one month, regardless of the department.

items.q: What notice will I get?
items.a: The policy states a one-month period to transition out. Details should be discussed with HR.

items.q: Do I need to inform HR if I am getting married to a colleague?
items.a: Yes. Inform HR so that the transition can be planned within the stipulated time.

items.q: My brother already works in the same company. Will I be removed?
items.a: Current employees who are blood relatives and work within the same department or organization are exempt from this policy.

items.q: Does the exemption apply forever?
items.a: The exemption covers existing blood relatives. However, any changes in roles, reassignments or future hiring involving blood relatives follow the policy.

items.q: Can my existing relative and I be moved into the same team?
items.a: No. Any change in role or reassignment must follow the guidelines of the policy.

items.q: Can another relative of mine be hired now, since my brother and I are already here?
items.a: No. Future hiring involving blood relatives follows the policy guidelines.

items.q: What if my relative is promoted to be my manager?
items.a: Changes in roles and reassignments follow the policy, so it would not be allowed if it violates the guidelines.

items.q: What if I hide that a candidate is my relative?
items.a: Violation of this policy can lead to disciplinary action up to termination for the involved parties.

items.q: Should I disclose if a candidate is my relative?
items.a: Yes. Please inform HR as early as possible so that the policy is applied correctly.

items.q: Who is punished if the policy is violated: the employee or the relative?
items.a: The policy states disciplinary action for the involved parties.

items.q: Is this policy only for new hiring or also internal transfers?
items.a: It also applies to changes in roles and reassignments.

items.q: Is this policy required by law?
items.a: The policy states that in some cases nepotism policies or employment laws restrict hiring of relatives, and violation can lead to legal complications.

items.q: Who do I contact for any doubt?
items.a: HR.

items.q: What is the PoSH Policy?
items.a: It is the Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Employees at the Workplace Policy of Prayosha Food Services Pvt. Ltd. (Petpooja). It aims to give every employee a workplace free of sexual harassment and to provide a way to raise and resolve complaints.

items.q: What does PoSH stand for?
items.a: Prevention of Sexual Harassment.

items.q: Which law is this policy based on?
items.a: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 and its Rules, 2013.

items.q: What is the date of issue and effective date?
items.a: Both are 08.05.2026 (Policy Version 1.4).

items.q: Who authorized the policy?
items.a: The Board of Directors.

items.q: What is the company's stand on sexual harassment?
items.a: Zero tolerance. Petpooja will not tolerate any form of sexual harassment.

items.q: Is this policy a part of my service rules?
items.a: Yes. It forms an integral part of the service rules for all employees in India.

items.q: Does the policy create a contract?
items.a: No. It is not intended to create contractual obligations, and Petpooja may modify it in accordance with applicable laws.

items.q: Who is covered by this policy?
items.a: All categories of employees, including regular, temporary, ad hoc and daily wage employees, contractors, probationers, trainees, apprentices and co-workers, with or without pay.

items.q: Does it cover interns?
items.a: Yes. Trainees, apprentices and similar categories "called by any other such name" are covered.

items.q: Does it cover contract workers?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: Does it cover employees working at client sites?
items.a: Yes. The policy applies at the workplace or at client sites.

items.q: What if a third party or outsider harasses me at work?
items.a: Petpooja will take all necessary and reasonable steps, including initiating action with the third party's employer.

items.q: What if a client or business associate harasses me?
items.a: Petpooja will not tolerate it, and the policy applies to harassment by clients or any other business associates.

items.q: What is covered under "workplace"?
items.a: All offices and premises, official activities away from premises, social, business or other functions where conduct may affect workplace relations, any place visited during employment, transportation provided by the employer, hotels and guest houses where you stay for work, and online communication tools provided by Petpooja.

items.q: Does it cover harassment during an office party?
items.a: Yes, if the conduct or comments may have an adverse impact on the workplace or workplace relations.

items.q: Does it cover harassment on official tours?
items.a: Yes. Any place visited as part of employment, including hotels and guest houses.

items.q: Does it cover harassment through email or Zoom?
items.a: Yes. Online communication such as emails, chatrooms and video conferencing is part of the workplace.

items.q: Does it cover company cab or transport?
items.a: Yes. Transportation provided by the employer is part of the workplace.

items.q: Does it apply to every office, regardless of the number of women employees?
items.a: Yes. Every unit or office in India is a workplace, irrespective of the number of female employees.

items.q: What is sexual harassment under the policy?
items.a: Any unwelcome behavior, direct or implied, such as physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favors, sexually colored remarks, showing pornography, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

items.q: What circumstances make it sexual harassment?
items.a: If it is connected with a promise of preferential treatment, threat of detrimental treatment, threat about employment status, interference with work or creating an intimidating, offensive or hostile environment, or humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety.

items.q: Is a sexual joke harassment?
items.a: Yes. Inappropriate or sexist jokes, loaded comments and sexual anecdotes are included.

items.q: Is staring at someone harassment?
items.a: Yes. Leering or staring in a sexually suggestive or offensive manner is included.

items.q: Is whistling harassment?
items.a: Yes. The policy lists whistling.

items.q: Are comments on appearance or clothing harassment?
items.a: Yes. Sexual comments about appearance, clothing or body parts are included.

items.q: Is inappropriate touching harassment?
items.a: Yes. This includes pinching, patting, rubbing or purposefully brushing up against another person.

items.q: Are WhatsApp messages with a sexual tone harassment?
items.a: Yes. Messages, SMS, WhatsApp, emails, phone calls, letters and gestures of a sexual nature are included.

items.q: Is asking about family planning or pregnancy harassment?
items.a: Yes. Asking sexual or gender-related questions, such as about sexual history, sexual orientation, family planning and pregnancy is included.

items.q: Are offensive comments on gender identity or sexual orientation harassment?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: Are gender stereotypes harassment?
items.a: Gender-biased statements and inappropriate stereotypes about women or men are included.

items.q: Is treating someone differently because of gender harassment?
items.a: Yes. Treating individuals differently based on gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, or pregnancy is included.

items.q: Is spreading rumours about someone's relationship harassment?
items.a: Yes. Spreading rumors about an employee's sexual relationship is included.

items.q: Is repeatedly asking someone to spend time after work harassment?
items.a: Yes, if the requests are repeated and unwelcome, as sexual propositions or requests for sexual favors.

items.q: Is helping someone harass another person also a violation?
items.a: Yes. Abetment to any of the acts is included.

items.q: What is sexual assault under the policy?
items.a: When an employee uses the body or any part of it, or any object as an extension of the body, in relation to another person without consent or against their will for a sexual purpose.

items.q: Is showing pornography harassment?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: Is displaying inappropriate sexual images at work harassment?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: Are inappropriate sexual sounds or gestures harassment?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: What is virtual sexual harassment?
items.a: Harassment through online platforms, such as inappropriate messages, content and conduct during virtual meetings.

items.q: Is taking screenshots of a colleague during a meeting harassment?
items.a: Yes. Taking screenshots of women colleagues during a meeting is listed.

items.q: Is sharing explicit photos without consent harassment?
items.a: Yes, including posting on social media or sharing on WhatsApp.

items.q: Is commenting on someone's social media handle harassment?
items.a: Personal comments on a person's social media handles are listed.

items.q: Is receiving unwelcome content about myself online harassment?
items.a: Yes. A woman receiving unwelcome material or content posted about her is listed.

items.q: Is using derogatory gender-based terms online harassment?
items.a: Yes.

items.q: Is not maintaining a dress code in video calls harassment?
items.a: Yes. Not maintaining a dress code during video conferences is listed.

items.q: Can my manager force me to join a "night suit" Zoom party?
items.a: No. Managers compelling employees to join 'night suit' Zoom parties is listed as harassment.

items.q: Are rumours about someone's sexuality harassment?
items.a: Yes. Comments or rumors about the victim's sexuality or sexual activities are listed.

items.q: What is the ICC?
items.a: The Internal Complaints Committee, formed as per the Act, which handles inquiries and redressal of sexual harassment complaints at each unit or location.

items.q: Who are the ICC members?
items.a: Helly Gandhi (Presiding Officer), Dinesh Prajapati, Naitik Shah, Janaki Dulla, Jatan Vala, Grishma Shah (members), and Shivani Madan Bose (External Panel Member).

items.q: How can I contact the Presiding Officer?
items.a: Helly Gandhi: helly.gandhi@petpooja.com, 8155098887.

items.q: How can I contact the other ICC members?
items.a: Dinesh Prajapati: dinesh.prajapati@petpooja.com, 8155009531. Naitik Shah: naitik.shah@petpooja.com, 6358987981. Janaki Dulla: janaki.dulla@petpooja.com, 9974014482. Jatan Vala: jatan.vala@petpooja.com, 9099078921. Grishma Shah: grishma.shah@petpooja.com, 7878491118.

items.q: Who is the external panel member?
items.a: Shivani Madan Bose, contact info@proudhr.com, 8866044877.

items.q: How is the ICC formed?
items.a: A minimum 4-member committee at every location, with a woman senior employee as Presiding Officer, two employee members committed to women's causes or with social work or legal knowledge, and one member from an NGO or familiar with sexual harassment issues. At least half the members must be women.

items.q: How long is an ICC member's tenure?
items.a: Not exceeding 3 years.

items.q: What if a member leaves?
items.a: The vacancy must be filled as quickly as possible and within 15 days.

items.q: What is the quorum of the ICC?
items.a: 4 members, including the Presiding Officer and at least two members, one of whom must be a woman.

items.q: Does the ICC submit any report?
items.a: Yes. An annual report each calendar year to management and the district officer, with complaints filed and disposed of, awareness programmes held and actions taken.

items.q: Who can file a complaint?
items.a: Any complainant, i.e. an employee who alleges that she has been subjected to sexual harassment at the workplace, in writing to the ICC.

items.q: Can a co-worker file a complaint for me?
items.a: Yes. Any woman employee or her co-worker may file a complaint with the ICC.

items.q: What is the time limit to file a complaint?
items.a: Within three months of the incident, or within three months of the last incident in a series.

items.q: What if I could not file within three months?
items.a: The ICC may extend the time for reasons recorded in writing if there were unavoidable circumstances.

items.q: I cannot write the complaint. What can I do?
items.a: The Presiding Officer or any ICC member will give all reasonable assistance to put your complaint in writing.

items.q: What if I am physically unable to file?
items.a: Your relative, friend, co-worker, an officer of the National or State Commission for Women, or any person with knowledge of the incident can file with your written consent.

items.q: What if I am mentally unable to file?
items.a: Your relative or friend, a special educator, a qualified psychiatrist or psychologist, your guardian, or a person with knowledge of the incident (jointly with those persons) can file.

items.q: Can I file a police complaint too?
items.a: Yes. Inform management and it will provide necessary assistance to file a complaint for any offence under the IPC.

items.q: What should my complaint include?
items.a: All material and relevant details of the alleged harassment, including the name of the respondent.

items.q: Is my complaint confidential?
items.a: Yes. The information is confidential and shared only with those who have a legitimate need to know.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: How do I file a complaint?
items.a: Submit it in writing to the ICC, by letter or email to the ICC members, with supporting documents and names and addresses of witnesses.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: How many copies of the complaint are needed?
items.a: 6 copies, with supporting documents.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Can I send it by email?
items.a: Yes, to the email IDs of the ICC members.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: What does the ICC do after receiving my complaint?
items.a: Within 7 days, it sends a copy to the respondent and informs you in writing about the initial steps taken.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: How long does the respondent have to reply?
items.a: Within 10 working days from the receipt of the documents, with a list of documents and witnesses.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: How is the inquiry conducted?
items.a: The ICC ensures a fair and just investigation. Both parties are heard separately first, witnesses are heard, and natural justice, including cross-examination, is followed.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: How long does the inquiry take?
items.a: Not more than 90 days from the date of commencement.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Can I bring a lawyer?
items.a: No. Parties cannot bring a legal practitioner to represent them at any stage before the ICC.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Will I be informed about the outcome?
items.a: Yes. The complainant and the respondent are informed of the outcome.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: What if neither party appears for the inquiry?
items.a: The ICC can terminate the proceedings after giving notice to both parties.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Are witnesses protected?
items.a: Yes. The ICC ensures care is taken to avoid any retaliation against witnesses.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Can the parties threaten witnesses?
items.a: No. Both the complainant and the respondent must refrain from any form of threat, intimidation or influencing of witnesses.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: Can I settle through conciliation?
items.a: Yes. Before an inquiry, at the complainant's request, the ICC can try to settle the matter through conciliation. No monetary settlement can be the basis.

items.s: How to File and What Happens Next
items.q: What happens if the matter is settled?
items.a: The ICC records the settlement, sends it to management and gives copies to both parties. No further inquiry is conducted.

items.q: Is there any relief while the inquiry is going on?
items.a: Yes. The ICC may recommend that the complainant or the respondent be transferred to another workplace.

items.q: Can I get leave during the inquiry?
items.a: Yes. Up to 3 months of leave in addition to your regular leave entitlement can be granted to the complainant.

items.q: Can the respondent be stopped from assessing my work?
items.a: Yes. The ICC can recommend preventing the respondent from assessing the complainant's work performance.

items.q: Is there any other interim relief?
items.a: Yes. Any other relief the ICC considers appropriate.

items.q: What happens when the inquiry is complete?
items.a: The ICC submits its report to management within 10 days, and it is made available to the parties.

items.q: What action can be taken if the allegation is proved?
items.a: A written apology, warning, reprimand or censure, withholding promotion or increments, termination, counselling, community service, or salary deduction to compensate the complainant.

items.q: What if the allegations are not proved?
items.a: The ICC recommends that no action is required.

items.q: What if the complaint is found false or malicious?
items.a: Action may be recommended, including disciplinary action.

items.q: Will I be punished if I could not prove my complaint?
items.a: No. A mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof is not grounds for action against the complainant.

items.q: What if a witness gives false evidence?
items.a: Disciplinary action can be taken against witnesses who give false evidence or produce forged or misleading documents.

items.q: How soon must management act on the recommendation?
items.a: Within 60 days of receipt.

items.q: What does the ICC report include?
items.a: Whether the conduct was sexual or derogatory, whether findings are based on evidence, credibility of parties and witnesses, previous accounts of harassment by the respondent, and whether both parties were heard.

items.q: Can I appeal against the ICC's decision?
items.a: Yes. A person aggrieved by the recommendations or their non-implementation may appeal to the court or tribunal as per the service rules or applicable law.

items.q: Will I face retaliation if I complain?
items.a: No. Regardless of the outcome, complainants, witnesses and those providing information are protected from retaliation if the complaint is in good faith.

items.q: What if the respondent pressures me during the inquiry?
items.a: Report it to the ICC as soon as possible. Disciplinary action will be taken if found genuine.

items.q: Who will know about my complaint?
items.a: Only those with a legitimate need to know. It will not be shared with the public, press or media.

items.q: What information is protected?
items.a: The contents of the complaint, identity and address of parties and witnesses, conciliation and inquiry proceedings, ICC recommendations and employer's actions.

items.q: What are my responsibilities as an employee?
items.a: Abstain from any acts of sexual harassment, report incidents without fear or favor, and help create an environment where co-workers can work without fear.

items.q: What are managers' responsibilities?
items.a: Provide a safe, non-hostile environment with proper lighting and safety, report complaints immediately, ensure no retaliation, implement disciplinary action, discuss PoSH periodically, maintain records, and support ICC training.

items.q: Should my manager report it if I tell him?
items.a: Yes. Managers must report any complaint or grievance immediately to the concerned authorities.

items.q: Where can I get more guidance?
items.a: From a Human Resources representative.

items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja can alter, add to, vary or substitute any provision at any time.

items.q: Who interprets the policy?
items.a: Petpooja, in its sole discretion.

items.q: A colleague keeps sending me inappropriate jokes on WhatsApp. What should I do?
items.a: Save the messages and submit a written complaint to the ICC within three months with supporting documents.

items.q: My manager said he will promote me if I go out with him. What do I do?
items.a: This is harassment (a promise of preferential treatment). Report it in writing to the ICC.

items.q: My manager threatened my job after I refused his advances. What do I do?
items.a: Report to the ICC in writing. Threat of detrimental treatment is harassment, and retaliation is not tolerated.

items.q: A client behaved inappropriately with me at his office. What should I do?
items.a: Report it to the ICC. The policy covers client sites and harassment by clients, and the company will act with the third party's employer.

items.q: I witnessed harassment of a colleague. What should I do?
items.a: Report it without fear or favour. A co-worker may file the complaint.

items.q: Is a male employee covered by this policy?
items.a: The policy is framed under the Act for women. All employees are asked to follow it. Please contact HR or the ICC for concerns involving other employees.

items.q: Can a man be the respondent?
items.a: Yes. The respondent is any person against whom the allegation of sexual harassment is made.

items.q: What if the respondent is a senior or a leader?
items.a: The policy applies to all. The ICC inquires under the same procedure.

items.q: Can the ICC interview my friends?
items.a: Yes. It can take testimonies of other relevant persons and review the evidence.

items.q: What is the Quarterly Team Get-Together Policy?
items.a: A policy that lets every team step away from targets and deadlines once a quarter to enjoy a meal together, celebrate work, and build trust and relationships.

items.q: Why do we have quarterly get-togethers?
items.a: To celebrate the work done together, get to know the people behind the roles, and build the trust that makes everyday collaboration easy.

items.q: Is the get-together compulsory?
items.a: Everyone is encouraged to join, but it is optional.

items.q: Is the get-together a work meeting?
items.a: No. It is about time together. No minutes or formal documentation are needed.

items.q: Who is responsible for organizing it?
items.a: Team leaders and city leads help their teams meet each quarter in line with this policy.

items.q: How often can my team meet?
items.a: Once in every quarter of the financial year.

items.q: What are the quarters?
items.a: Q1: April to June. Q2: July to September. Q3: October to December. Q4: January to March.

items.q: Which quarter are we in now (November 2026)?
items.a: Q3 (October to December).

items.q: Can we meet twice in the same quarter?
items.a: The policy allows one get-together per quarter per team.

items.q: Can I skip a quarter?
items.a: Yes, but the team should still meet once in that quarter using the combined budget if the budget is carried forward.

items.q: What if my team could not meet in a quarter?
items.a: The unused budget carries forward to the next quarter, and the team still meets once in that quarter with the combined budget.

items.q: How many people are needed for a get-together?
items.a: At least 3 colleagues.

items.q: We are only 2 colleagues in our town. Can we claim?
items.a: No. A minimum of 3 colleagues is required. Colleagues from nearby towns can join to complete the group.

items.q: Can colleagues from nearby towns join?
items.a: Yes, especially in smaller towns, to make up the group.

items.q: Can family members or friends join?
items.a: The policy talks about colleagues. Family and friends are not mentioned.

items.q: Can an outsider or client attend?
items.a: The policy is for colleagues. Please check with HR.

items.q: Can other teams join our get-together?
items.a: At Head Office, teams may meet on their own or together with other teams.

items.q: Can an intern attend?
items.a: The policy says everyone is encouraged to join. Please check with your team lead.

items.q: Where do we hold the get-together?
items.a: Teams choose a venue that is convenient, easy for everyone to reach and within the budget.

items.q: Can it be held during office hours?
items.a: No. It is held over lunch or dinner, outside regular work hours.

items.q: Can we have a get-together on a weekend?
items.a: Yes, it can be held outside regular working hours. Choose lunch or dinner.

items.q: Can we have breakfast or tea-time meeting?
items.a: The policy says lunch or dinner.

items.q: Can we pick a restaurant outside the city?
items.a: Get-togethers are held within the city. For outside Head Office, they are held within the city.

items.q: Can colleagues from other cities travel?
items.a: When a VP or CXO visits for the quarterly get-together, colleagues from nearby cities are welcome to travel and join on the company's expense.

items.q: How much is the budget?
items.a: From 1st October 2026, it is Rs. 1,000 per attendee per quarter, inclusive of all taxes.

items.q: What was the earlier budget?
items.a: Rs. 600 per attendee per quarter, for April to September 2026.

items.q: Does the budget include GST?
items.a: Yes. It is inclusive of all taxes.

items.q: What does the budget cover?
items.a: The meal, refreshments and any other arrangements.

items.q: Does it cover alcohol?
items.a: No. Alcohol is not part of the budget.

items.q: Does it cover travel cost?
items.a: No. Travel costs are not part of the budget (except company-covered travel when a VP/CXO visits).

items.q: What if our bill is more than the budget?
items.a: Only expenses within the allocated budget are reimbursed. The extra must be borne by the attendees.

items.q: We are 5 people. What is our budget for the quarter?
items.a: Rs. 5,000 (5 x Rs. 1,000) from October 2026.

items.q: We are 6 people. What is our budget in Q3?
Is the budget per attendee or per team?
items.a: Per attendee.

items.q: If we are 4 attendees and spent Rs. 3,500, how much will be reimbursed?
items.a: Rs. 3,500, because it is within the Rs. 4,000 budget.

items.q: If we are 4 attendees and spent Rs. 4,500, how much will be reimbursed?
items.a: Rs. 4,000. The remaining Rs. 500 is not reimbursed.

items.q: Can I count people who did not attend in the budget?
items.a: No. The budget is per attendee, and the claim lists the names of everyone who attended.

items.q: What if we don't use the budget in a quarter?
items.a: It carries forward to the next quarter.

items.q: How long can the budget carry forward?
items.a: Through the financial year, till 31 March.

items.q: What happens to unused budget at 31 March?
items.a: It closes and cannot be used afterward.

items.q: Our team did not meet in Q1 and Q2. What is our budget in Q3?
items.a: The unused April to September 2026 budget carries forward at the earlier rate of Rs. 600 per quarter per attendee, and the Q3 budget is at Rs. 1,000 per attendee. The team still meets once with the combined budget.

items.q: Does the carried-forward budget stay at Rs. 600?
items.a: Yes. Unused budget from April to September 2026 carries forward at the earlier rate of Rs. 600 per quarter.

items.q: Can we meet twice in Q4 to use the carried-forward budget?
items.a: The team still meets once in that quarter, with the combined budget.

items.q: If we don't meet in Q3, what will be our Q4 budget?
items.a: Q3 budget plus Q4 budget (Rs. 1,000 + Rs. 1,000 per attendee), used in one get-together in Q4.

items.a: Teams may meet on their own or together with other teams.

items.a: In each city, all teams meet together, brought together by the city lead.

items.a: The Sales BDM/ASM, Support or Training Manager in the city.

items.a: No. Outside Head Office, all teams in the city meet together.

items.a: They can join the get-together, and colleagues from nearby cities are welcome to travel and join at the company's expense.

items.a: The company.

items.q: Is the full amount reimbursed?
items.a: Expenses within the allocated budget are reimbursed in full.

items.q: How long do I have to submit the claim?

items.a: Claims are processed for up to 40 days from the get-together date. Late claims may not be processed.

items.q: What happens if I forget to claim?
items.a: The claim may lapse after 40 days from the get-together.
