items.q: Our team is in Ahmedabad Head Office. Can we meet with another team?
items.a: Yes. At Head Office, teams may meet on their own or together with other teams.

items.q: Does the policy apply to all employees?
items.a: It applies to teams; everyone is encouraged to join.

items.q: Is the budget in effect from the start of the financial year?
items.a: The Rs. 1,000 budget is in effect from 1st October 2026. Earlier it was Rs. 600.

items.q: Can I use the budget for gifts or decorations?
items.a: The budget is meant for food and refreshments. It also covers "any other arrangements", but travel and alcohol are excluded.

items.q: Can I use the budget for a cake?
items.a: Yes, as part of food and refreshments, within the budget.

items.q: Is attendance recorded?
items.a: The claim includes the names of everyone who attended.

items.q: Can a team lead ask me to attend?
items.a: Attendance is optional. Everyone is encouraged to join.

items.q: Is the policy going to change?
items.a: It may be reviewed and updated from time to time in line with business requirements.

items.q: Whom do I ask if I am unsure about the venue?
items.a: Your team leader or city lead.

items.q: Can we get-together over a lunch on a working day?
items.a: It must be outside regular work hours. A lunch break during office hours is not what the policy intends.

items.q: Is the get-together held every quarter for sure?
items.a: Each team can meet once in every quarter. If a team cannot, the budget carries forward.

items.q: We are three people in a small town. Can we hold the get-together?
items.a: Yes. A minimum of 3 colleagues is required.

items.q: We are two people in a small town. What can we do?
items.a: Join colleagues from a nearby town to complete the group of at least 3.

items.q: Who invites the people in the city?
items.a: The city lead brings everyone together.

items.q: Does the budget include tips?
items.a: The budget is inclusive of all taxes and covers the meal, refreshments and other arrangements. Tips are not specifically mentioned.

items.q: Can I split the bill across two restaurants?
items.a: The policy is for one get-together per quarter at a convenient venue. Please check with HR.

items.q: What if someone attended but I forgot to add the name?
items.a: Claims need names of everyone who attended. Add all names before submission.

items.q: Is there a limit on the number of attendees?
items.a: No upper limit is mentioned. The budget is per attendee.

items.q: When did the Rs. 1,000 rate start?
items.a: 1st October 2026.

items.q: What is the difference between the Rs. 600 and Rs. 1,000 budgets?
items.a: Rs. 600 applied before 1st October 2026. Rs. 1,000 applies from 1st October 2026.

items.q: What if my team has already used the Q3 budget at the old rate?
items.a: Expenses in Q3 are as per the new rate from 1st October 2026. Please check with HR for any clarifications.

items.q: Can I claim the get-together under another expense head?
items.a: No. Claim it on GreytHR under this policy.

items.q: Does the VP or CXO's meal also count under the budget?
items.a: The budget is per attendee, so the visiting VP or CXO can be counted as an attendee. Please confirm with HR.

items.q: Are drinks like juices or soft drinks covered?
items.a: Yes. Food and refreshments are covered. Alcohol is not.

items.q: Are hotel stays for outstation colleagues covered?
items.a: Travel costs are not part of the budget. The company bears travel only when a VP or CXO visits.

items.q: Who reimburses the claim?
items.a: It is processed through GreytHR by the company, as per the policy.

items.q: Can I submit multiple claims for one get-together?
items.a: Submit one claim with the names of everyone who attended.

items.q: Is it okay if we hold the get-together on the last day of the quarter?
items.a: Yes, as long as it is within the quarter and claims are submitted within 40 days.

items.q: What if the get-together date is in March and I claim in April?
items.a: Claim within 40 days of the get-together. The budget runs with the financial year and closes on 31 March.

items.q: Do remote employees get the budget?
items.a: Remote employees can join the get-togethers in their city. The city lead brings everyone together.

items.q: Do we need approval before holding the get-together?
items.a: The policy does not require prior approval. Team leaders and city leads help teams meet.

items.q: Can we hold the get-together online?
items.a: The policy describes lunch or dinner together. Online meetings are not mentioned.

items.q: Do I need to attend if I am on leave?
items.a: No. Attendance is optional.

items.q: What if the venue is expensive?
items.a: Choose a venue within the budget. Anything beyond the budget is not reimbursed.

items.q: Who decides the venue?
items.a: The team chooses a venue that is convenient and within the budget.

items.q: Is it a good idea to invite other teams?
items.a: At Head Office teams may meet together. Outside Head Office, all teams in the city meet together.

items.q: Is this policy for the full year?
items.a: It covers the four quarters of each financial year (April to March).

items.q: Is there any other documentation like photos required?
items.a: No. No minutes or formal documentation are needed.

items.q: What is the first thing I should do to plan one?
items.a: Talk to your team leader or city lead, fix a date within the quarter, choose a venue within budget and tell colleagues.

items.q: Can we use the budget for a team lunch during a festival?
items.a: Yes, if it is the quarterly get-together outside regular work hours and within the budget.

items.q: Can we club two quarters' get-together into one?
items.a: Yes. If a team cannot meet in a quarter, unused budget carries forward, and the team meets once in the next quarter with the combined budget.

items.q: Is the get-together applicable to every employee?
items.a: Each team can meet once every quarter, and everyone is encouraged to join.

items.q: What is the Employee Referral Bonus Policy?
items.a: A program that rewards employees who refer candidates for job openings in the company.

items.q: Why does the company have this policy?
items.a: To attract the right candidates by involving existing employees.

items.q: What is the effective date?
items.a: 1-06-2026 (Draft Version 1.5).

items.q: How much is the referral bonus?
items.a: Rs. 5,000 per candidate.

items.q: Is there a limit on how many people I can refer?
items.a: No. There is no limit on the number of referrals.

items.q: Is the referral amount taxable?
items.a: Yes. It is subject to applicable taxes.

items.q: Who is eligible to get a referral bonus?
items.a: All regular employees of the company, except HR employees, the senior management team and the hiring manager of the particular vacancy.

items.q: I work in HR. Can I get a referral bonus?
items.a: No. HR employees are excluded.

items.q: I am part of the senior management. Can I get a bonus?
items.a: No. The senior management team is excluded.

items.q: I am the hiring manager for an opening. Can I refer someone for it?
items.a: You can, but you will not get the bonus for that vacancy.

items.q: I am a hiring manager of a different team. Can I get the bonus for referring someone to another team's opening?
items.a: The exclusion is for the hiring manager of that particular vacancy. For other vacancies, you may be eligible.

items.q: Can an intern refer a candidate?
items.a: The policy applies to regular employees. Interns are not mentioned.

items.q: Can a contract employee refer?
items.a: The policy applies to regular employees. Please check with HR for contract staff.

items.q: Can I refer someone in my probation period?
items.a: The policy applies to all regular employees. Please check with HR for probationers.

items.q: How do I refer a candidate?
items.a: Share the candidate's resume with HR through the KLIMB portal only by signing in at https://hire.klimb.io/employee-signup.

items.q: Can I email the resume to HR?
items.a: No. Referrals must be submitted only via the KLIMB portal.

items.q: Can I give the resume to the recruiter on WhatsApp?
items.a: No. Only KLIMB referrals are counted.

items.q: How long is a referred resume valid?
items.a: 3 months.

items.q: Where can I see the job openings?
items.a: Job openings are posted on the company's social media page and circulated through internal email by HR.

items.q: What is my role after referring?
items.a: Only submitting the resume. Interview and other formalities follow the normal recruitment process.

items.q: Can I attend the interview of my referral?
items.a: No. The recruiter coordinates with the referred candidate. Your role is limited to submitting the resume.

items.q: Can I influence the selection of my referral?
items.a: No. Selection depends on merit, and the referral goes through the normal interview process.

items.q: Does a referral mean the candidate is selected?
items.a: No. Making a referral does not mean final selection.

items.q: Who coordinates the interview?
items.a: The recruiter coordinates with the referred candidate.

items.q: When will I get my Rs. 5,000?
items.a: After the referred candidate completes 3 months from the date of joining.

items.q: How will I be paid?
items.a: The amount is processed after the completed month's payroll.

items.q: My referral joined on 1st January. When do I get the bonus?
items.a: After 3 months, i.e. after 1st April, processed after that completed month's payroll.

items.q: What if the referred candidate leaves within 3 months?
items.a: No referral bonus is paid.

items.q: What if I resign before the 3 months of my referral are completed?
items.a: No bonus is paid. Both the employee and the referred candidate must be active on the payroll.

items.q: Do both of us need to be on the payroll?
items.a: Yes. Both the existing employee and the referred candidate must be active employees to receive the bonus.

items.q: Who initiates the payment?
items.a: The recruiter sends the details to HR after 3 months of joining.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: When will I not get the referral bonus?
items.a: If the candidate's resume already exists in the company's databank, if the candidate applied before your referral, if the referred candidate works under you, if you resign during the referral period, if the candidate is a relative, or if the referral came through a recruitment agency.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: The candidate already exists in the company database. Will I get the bonus?
items.a: No.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: The candidate had applied before I referred him. Will I get the bonus?
items.a: No.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Can I refer my brother or relative?
items.a: No. The referred candidate should not be your relative.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Can I refer my friend?
items.a: Yes. The referral should be from your contacts and the candidate should not be a relative.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: The referred candidate will work under me. Do I get the bonus?
items.a: No. If the referred candidate has to work under the employee who referred them, no referral is paid.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Can I refer someone through a recruitment agency?
items.a: No. No referral should be made with the help of any recruitment agency.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Two employees referred the same candidate. Who gets the bonus?
items.a: The employee who referred first.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Can I refer a candidate who was rejected earlier?
items.a: If the resume already exists in the databank, no bonus will be paid.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: My referral was rejected. Can I refer again for another post?
items.a: Yes, as long as the resume is not already in the databank. Please check with HR.

items.s: Conditions Where No Bonus Is Paid
items.q: Do I get a bonus if my referral is hired after 3 months?
items.a: The resume is valid for 3 months. If the hiring happens after that, no referral bonus is payable.

items.q: How do I earn Rs. 5,000?
items.a: Refer a non-relative candidate on the KLIMB portal, who is not already in the databank and clears the selection process, joins, and completes 3 months while both of you are on the payroll.

items.q: Can I get a bonus for two candidates?
items.a: Yes. Each selected candidate who meets the conditions earns Rs. 5,000.

items.q: I referred a friend and he got selected. When do I get my money?
items.a: After he completes 3 months from the joining date.

items.q: What if my friend joins and then moves to another department?
items.a: The condition is the candidate completing 3 months and both being active on payroll. Please check with HR if the move affects reporting to you.

items.q: What if my friend is in my department but does not report to me?
items.a: The restriction applies if the candidate has to work under you. Please check with HR for team members who are not under you.

items.q: What if my friend's resume was already with a recruiter before?
items.a: If it exists in the databank, no referral bonus is paid.

items.q: Is KLIMB the same as the platform for IJT?
items.a: Yes. KLIMB is also the platform where employees apply for Internal Job Transfers.

items.q: Can I refer for any position?
items.a: You can refer for open positions posted by the company.

items.q: Does the policy cover referral for HR vacancies?
items.a: HR employees are excluded from the bonus. Others can refer for HR vacancies.

items.q: Will I be informed if my referral is selected?
items.a: The referred candidate is notified by the recruiter. Check with HR for updates.

items.q: Who do I contact for referral-related queries?
items.a: The HR/Recruitment team.

items.q: Can the company change this policy?
items.a: Yes. The company can revise or modify any or all clauses depending upon business demand.

items.q: Does the referral policy apply to senior positions?
items.a: It applies to open positions, and the bonus amount is Rs. 5,000 per candidate.

items.q: Is the referral bonus the same for every role?
items.a: Yes. Rs. 5,000 per candidate.

items.q: How do I make sure I am the first referrer?
items.a: Submit the resume on the KLIMB portal as early as possible. The first referrer gets preference.

items.q: What is KLIMB?
items.a: The portal through which employees share resumes of referred candidates with HR.

items.q: Where do I sign up for referrals?
items.a: At https://hire.klimb.io/employee-signup.

items.q: Do I need an account on KLIMB to refer?
items.a: Yes. You must sign in on the KLIMB employee sign-up page.

items.q: Can HR employees refer candidates?
items.a: They can share candidates, but they are not eligible for the bonus.

items.q: I referred a candidate, but HR already had the resume. What now?
items.a: No referral bonus is payable if the resume already exists in the company's databank.

items.q: What does "candidate applied before the referral" mean?
items.a: If the candidate applied directly to the company before you referred them, no referral amount is paid.

items.q: How will I know if my referral resume is valid?
items.a: A referred resume is valid for 3 months from submission.

items.q: What if my referred candidate gets an offer after 4 months?
items.a: The resume is valid for 3 months. After that, the referral may not be considered.

items.q: Is the referral amount paid with salary?
items.a: It is processed after the completed month's payroll.

items.q: My referred candidate completed 3 months on the 15th. When will I get paid?
items.a: The amount will be processed after the completed month's payroll.

items.q: Can I get the bonus if I leave the company after my referral completes 3 months?
items.a: The condition is that both of you are on the payroll through the referral period. Once the period is complete and you are still on the payroll for payment, you are eligible. Please check with HR for timing.

items.q: Is the bonus paid in advance?
items.a: No. It is paid only after 3 months from the date of joining.

items.q: Who tells HR to pay my bonus?
items.a: The recruiter sends details to HR after 3 months of joining.

items.q: Can I refer my spouse?
items.a: No. The referred candidate should not be your relative.

items.q: Can I refer my cousin?
items.a: No. The referred candidate should not be related to you.

items.q: Can I refer my college friend?
items.a: Yes, if they are from your contacts and not a relative.

items.q: Can I refer someone from social media?
items.a: The referral should come from your contacts. Candidates found through recruitment agencies are not eligible.

items.q: Can I forward a job opening to my contacts?
items.a: Yes. You can share the company's job openings with your contacts and then refer through KLIMB.

items.q: How do I know about open positions?
items.a: Through the company's social media page and internal emails circulated by HR.

items.q: Does the referral policy apply to freshers?
items.a: Yes, for any open position, subject to the same conditions.

items.q: What if my referral fails the interview?
items.a: No bonus. Selection depends on merit.

items.q: What if my referral was selected but did not join?
items.a: No bonus. The bonus is paid only after the candidate joins and completes 3 months.

items.q: What if my referral joined and left in 2 months?
items.a: No bonus.

items.q: Will I get the bonus if my referral is on notice period at 3 months?
items.a: The policy requires the candidate to be an active employee on payroll. Please check with HR.

items.q: Can I refer someone who worked in the company earlier?
items.a: If the resume is in the company databank, no referral is paid. Rehire is also governed by the Rehire Policy.

items.q: Is referring through a consultant allowed?
items.a: No. Referrals made with the help of any recruitment agency are not allowed.

items.q: If two people refer the same candidate on the same day, who gets it?
items.a: The employee who referred first gets preference.

items.q: What if I referred first but the candidate used another employee's reference?
items.a: The first referral recorded on the KLIMB portal gets preference.

items.q: Is there a maximum bonus I can earn in a year?
items.a: No. There is no limit on the number of referrals.

items.q: Will the company deduct tax from my referral amount?
items.a: The referral amount is subject to applicable taxes.

items.q: Do I get a bonus if I refer a candidate for an internship?
items.a: The policy mentions candidates for job openings. Please check with HR for internships.

items.q: Can I check the status of my referral?
items.a: Yes, through the KLIMB portal or by contacting the recruiter or HR.

items.q: What is the benchmark role of the referrer?
items.a: The referrer's role is limited to depositing the resume, to keep the process fair.

items.q: Can my referral get special treatment in the interview?
items.a: No. The referred candidate goes through the normal interview and selection process.

items.q: Do I need to be present on the payroll when my referral joins?
items.a: Yes. Both of you must be active employees on the payroll.

items.q: What if I move to another team and my referral then reports to me?
items.a: If the referred candidate has to work under you, no referral is paid.

items.q: What if I am promoted to the hiring manager of that department?
items.a: You are excluded from the bonus as the hiring manager for that vacancy.

items.q: Is referral of a candidate for a vacancy in my own team allowed?
items.a: Yes. But if the candidate will work under you, no bonus is paid.

items.q: Who verifies the bonus?
items.a: The recruiter and HR.

items.q: Does the Rs. 5,000 change by designation?
items.a: No. It is Rs. 5,000 per candidate.

items.q: Is the Referral Policy still in draft?
items.a: It is Draft Version 1.5, effective 1-06-2026.

items.q: Can I refer more than one person for the same opening?
items.a: Yes. There is no limit on referrals, and each selected candidate who meets the conditions earns Rs. 5,000.

items.q: Is the bonus paid if the referred candidate is hired on a contract?
items.a: The policy says the candidate must be on the company's payroll and complete 3 months. Please check with HR for contract hires.

items.q: Do I need approval from my manager to refer someone?
items.a: No. Submit the resume on the KLIMB portal.

items.q: What is the Employee Rehire Policy?
items.a: It explains who can be rehired by Petpooja after leaving, and how the rehire process, salary and onboarding work.

items.q: What is the effective date?
items.a: 1-04-2023 (Draft Version 1.1).

items.q: Can a former employee come back to Petpooja?
items.a: Yes, if they left for an eligible reason and their performance at Petpooja was satisfactory.

items.q: Is rehire guaranteed for eligible people?
items.a: No. Eligible employees can be considered. HR checks eligibility, qualifications and the position they apply for.

items.q: Which former employees can be considered for rehire?
items.a: Those who left through voluntary resignation, company lay-offs due to business needs, or expired contract, with satisfactory performance.

items.q: I resigned from the company. Can I be rehired?
items.a: Yes, if your performance was satisfactory, after a minimum gap of one year from separation.

items.q: I was laid off due to business needs. Can I be rehired?
items.a: Yes, if your performance was satisfactory, after a minimum gap of one year.

items.q: My contract expired. Can I come back?
items.a: Yes. You can ask for a contract renewal immediately and the company may consider it.

items.q: Do contract employees also need a one-year gap?
items.a: No. The one-year gap excludes employees whose contracts expired. They can ask for renewal immediately.

items.q: How long should I wait before reapplying after resignation?
items.a: At least one year after your separation from Petpooja.

items.q: I resigned 8 months ago. Can I apply now?
items.a: No. You need a minimum gap of one year.

items.q: I left exactly one year ago. Can I apply?
items.a: Yes. The minimum gap is one year after separation.

items.q: Is satisfactory performance compulsory?
items.a: Yes. The performance at Petpooja should have been satisfactory.

items.q: How will HR check my performance?
items.a: Based on your previous performance records and evaluations.

items.q: Who is not eligible for rehire?
items.a: Employees terminated for violating company policies or for illegal or unethical behavior, terminated for an unsatisfactory rating in the most recent performance evaluation, those who abandoned their job, and those who did not show up on the first day after accepting an offer.

items.q: I was terminated for policy violation. Can I return?
items.a: In general, no.

items.q: I was terminated for illegal or unethical behavior. Can I return?
items.a: In general, no.

items.q: I was terminated because of a low performance rating. Can I return?
items.a: In general, no.

items.q: I abandoned my job. Can I be rehired?
items.a: In general, no. Job abandonment is a reason for non-eligibility.

items.q: I accepted an offer but did not join. Can I apply again?
items.a: In general, no. Not showing up on the first day after accepting an offer makes you not eligible for rehire.

items.q: Is the "not eligible" rule absolute?
items.a: The policy says such employees "will, in general, not be considered". Exceptions would need HR and management decisions.

items.q: I resigned but my last performance rating was low. Can I return?
items.a: The policy requires satisfactory performance. A low rating may affect eligibility. HR decides.

items.q: I left without serving my notice period. Can I be rehired?
items.a: The policy does not list this directly. HR will check the reason and your performance.

items.q: Will I be treated as a new hire if I am rehired?
items.a: If you worked for less than 12 months, yes. You go through the hiring and onboarding process like a new hire.

items.q: What will my salary be if I worked less than 12 months earlier?
items.a: You come back on the same salary you were last drawing at Petpooja.

items.q: What if I worked more than 12 months earlier?
items.a: You may also go through the hiring and onboarding process, and your salary will be negotiated.

items.q: Can I negotiate my salary if I was here for 2 years?
items.a: Yes. For former employees with more than 12 months, salary is negotiated.

items.q: Can I negotiate my salary if I was here for 8 months?
items.a: No. You come back on the same salary you last drew.

items.q: What if I have been away for more than 1 year?
items.a: You are considered a new hire in any case.

items.q: Will my previous years of service count?
items.a: The policy says employees away for more than a year are considered new hires. The policy does not provide for counting earlier service.

items.q: Will my old leave balance come back?
items.a: The policy does not provide for it. Rehired employees are generally treated as new hires.

items.q: Will my probation apply again?
items.a: Employees treated as new hires go through the hiring and onboarding process. Please check with HR regarding probation.

items.q: Can I get my old designation back?
items.a: It depends on the position you apply for and your qualification. HR and the hiring manager decide.

items.q: Is the salary negotiation based on market?
items.a: The policy says it will be negotiated. HR and management decide.

items.q: How do I apply for rehire?
items.a: Apply to an open position at Petpooja. HR will verify your eligibility.

items.q: Who verifies if I am eligible?
items.a: HR.

items.q: What is the procedure if I worked for less than 12 months?
items.a: HR verifies eligibility, you go through the standard hiring procedure, and if rehired, the standard onboarding.

items.q: What is the procedure if I worked for more than 12 months?
items.a: HR verifies eligibility, then you go through a pre-employment assessment or pre-screening and an interview. If rehired, you go through the custom re-boarding program.

items.q: Will I have to take an interview again?
items.a: Yes. At least an assessment/pre-screening and an interview are required for those with more than 12 months of service.

items.q: What is the re-boarding program?
items.a: A custom onboarding program for rehired employees with more than 12 months of previous service.

items.q: Is standard onboarding applicable to me?
items.a: If you worked less than 12 months earlier, yes.

items.q: Do I need to be qualified for the position?
items.a: Yes. You must be eligible and qualified for the position you apply to.

items.q: Will my previous manager's feedback matter?
items.a: Your previous performance at Petpooja matters for eligibility.

items.q: Can I apply for any position?
items.a: Yes, an open position where you are qualified.

items.q: I resigned 14 months ago after 3 years. Can I apply?
items.a: Yes. You are eligible after one year with satisfactory performance. You will be treated as a new hire since you have been away for more than a year, with a negotiated salary.

items.q: I resigned 6 months ago and worked here for 10 months. Can I return?
items.a: Not yet. You need a one-year gap. After that, you would be considered a new hire.

items.q: My contract ended last month. Can I come back right now?
items.a: Yes. Contract-expired employees can ask for contract renewal immediately.

items.q: I left on good terms after 5 years. Will my salary be the same as before?
items.a: No. The salary will be negotiated.

items.q: Can I refer myself on the Referral Policy?
items.a: No. Referrals are for other candidates.

items.q: Is rehire the same as an Internal Job Transfer?
items.a: No. IJT is for current employees. Rehire is for former employees.

items.q: I was laid off in 2023. Can I apply now?
items.a: Yes, if you left due to business needs and your performance was satisfactory.

items.q: I left for a better job but the new job was not good. Can I return?
items.a: Yes, if you resigned voluntarily with satisfactory performance, after the one-year gap.

items.q: Does rehire need approval from management?
items.a: HR verifies eligibility, and the hiring process is followed. Management approval is part of the hiring process.

items.q: Whom do I contact?
items.a: The HR department.

items.q: Can I rejoin Petpooja?
items.a: Yes, if you left via resignation, lay-off due to business needs or contract expiry, your performance was satisfactory, and you meet the one-year gap (not required for expired contracts).

items.q: I want to rejoin. What should I do?
items.a: Wait for the one-year gap to complete (if applicable), apply for an open position, and HR will verify your eligibility.

items.q: How many months should I wait to come back?
items.a: 12 months (one year) after separation, except for employees whose contracts expired.

items.q: I was a contract employee and my contract was not renewed. Can I come back?
items.a: Yes. You can ask for a contract renewal immediately and the company may consider it.

items.q: Will my previous salary be considered if I rejoin after 2 years?
items.a: You will be considered a new hire since you have been away for more than a year, and salary will be negotiated.

items.q: I was in the company for 6 months. What salary will I get on rejoining?
items.a: The same salary you were last drawing, if rehired within the one-year gap rules.

items.q: I was in the company for 11 months. Which rule applies?
items.a: Less than 12 months: you are treated as a new hire and come back on the last drawn salary.

items.q: I was in the company for exactly 12 months. Which rule applies?
items.a: The policy says "less than 12 months" and "more than 12 months". Please confirm with HR for exactly 12 months.

items.q: Are rehired employees given the same benefits?
items.a: The policy says they go through hiring and onboarding like new hires. Benefits follow the applicable policies.

items.q: Will I have to submit documents again?
items.a: Yes. As a new hire or rehire, you go through the onboarding process.

items.q: Is background verification needed again?
items.a: The policy mentions pre-employment assessment and standard hiring procedures. Please check with HR for verification details.

items.q: Can I be rehired into the same team?
items.a: It depends on the open position and the hiring manager's decision.

items.q: Does the one-year gap apply to layoffs?
items.a: Yes. The one-year gap applies to voluntary resignation and lay-offs. It does not apply to expired contracts.

items.q: What is meant by "company lay-offs due to business needs"?
items.a: Separation of employees for business reasons, not related to their performance or behaviour.

items.q: Will I be considered if I was retrenched?
items.a: Retrenchment is for reasons not relating to performance or behaviour. HR will consider your case based on this policy.

items.q: Can an employee terminated for poor performance rejoin later?
items.a: In general, no. Termination due to an unsatisfactory rating on the most recent performance evaluation makes you ineligible.

items.q: What if I abandoned my job due to a family emergency?
items.a: Job abandonment is a reason for non-eligibility. You may discuss your case with HR, but you will in general not be considered.

items.q: What if I had an unsatisfactory rating but I resigned?
items.a: The policy requires satisfactory performance for eligibility. HR will decide.

items.q: What does "satisfactory performance" mean?
items.a: A satisfactory or better performance rating while you worked at Petpooja.

items.q: Do I need to serve a notice period again?
items.a: Rehired employees are treated per their new employment terms. Please check with HR.

items.q: Will the company give me a joining bonus on rehire?
items.a: The policy does not mention any joining bonus.

items.q: Will I get a higher designation on rehire?
items.a: Based on the position applied for and your qualification. HR decides.

items.q: Do I need to go through a pre-employment assessment?
items.a: If you worked for more than 12 months, yes, along with an interview. If less than 12 months, you go through the standard hiring procedure.

items.q: What is the difference between standard hiring and re-boarding?
items.a: Standard hiring and onboarding is for those with less than 12 months of earlier service. Re-boarding is a custom program for those with more than 12 months.

items.q: If I was away for more than one year after working for 3 years, do I get re-boarding?
items.a: The policy says employees away for more than a year are considered new hires in any case.

items.q: Can I apply for rehire again if rejected?
items.a: Yes, for other open positions, as long as you remain eligible.

items.q: Who decides the final rehire?
items.a: HR and the hiring manager, through the hiring process.

items.q: Does the rehire policy apply to interns?
items.a: The policy does not mention interns.

items.q: Is rehire applicable to part-time employees?
items.a: The policy does not distinguish. Please check with HR.

items.q: Will my past leave encashment be considered?
items.a: Leave encashment is settled in Full and Final at the time of exit. It is not carried forward.

items.q: Will my earlier loan or advance dues affect rehire?
items.a: Dues must be cleared before separation. Pending dues can affect your relieving and may influence rehire.

items.q: Is there any appeal if I am marked not eligible?
items.a: The policy does not provide an appeal. You can talk to HR.

items.q: Can my referrer get a referral bonus if I am rehired?
items.a: Referral is not paid if the resume already exists in the company's databank.

items.q: Do I need to inform HR if my earlier manager is the hiring manager?
items.a: HR verifies eligibility. Your previous record is considered.

items.q: Is the policy applicable to all departments?
items.a: Yes. It applies to all former employees of Petpooja.

items.q: Can an employee who was terminated due to restructuring be rehired?
items.a: Yes, if the separation was due to business needs and performance was satisfactory.

items.q: Does the one-year gap start from my last working day?
items.a: It starts from your separation from Petpooja.

items.q: Can I get my old employee ID back?
items.a: The policy does not say. As a new hire, a new ID may be given. Check with HR.

items.q: What happens to my old service years in gratuity?
items.a: The rehire policy treats most rehires as new hires. Please check with HR and Accounts for gratuity.

items.q: Is rehire possible after job abandonment if the reason was medical?
items.a: In general no. Share the details with HR for a case review.

items.q: Can I apply to the company through a referral?
items.a: Yes, but if your resume already exists in the databank, no referral bonus is paid.

items.q: Where can I read the rehire policy?
items.a: From HR or the company policy folder.

items.q: Will HR inform me about the eligibility result?
items.a: HR verifies eligibility when you apply. You will be informed as part of the hiring process.

items.q: Does the company have to rehire me if I qualify?
items.a: No. Eligible employees "can be considered". It is not guaranteed.

items.q: Does the policy apply to employees who left during probation?
items.a: Yes, if the reason was resignation, lay-off or expired contract, and performance was satisfactory.

items.q: What if I resigned but did not complete my notice?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. HR will review your case.

items.q: What is a Salary Advance?
items.a: A facility that lets you draw your salary before the payday during a contingency.

items.q: Why does the company offer salary advance?
items.a: To help employees during exceptional personal emergencies.

items.q: What is the effective date of this policy?
items.a: 1-01-2026 (Draft Version 1.1).

items.q: Is salary advance the same as a loan?
items.a: No. A salary advance is recovered fully from the salary of the same month. A loan is repaid in EMIs under the Loan Policy.

items.q: Is salary advance my right?
items.a: No. It is allowed only in exceptional cases and is recommended by department heads very selectively.

items.q: Am I eligible for a salary advance?
items.a: If you are a confirmed full-time employee with at least six months of active employment at Petpooja and you have no running company loan, you can apply in an emergency.

items.q: I want a salary advance.
items.a: You can apply if you are a confirmed full-time employee with 6 months of service, you face a genuine unforeseen emergency, and you have no running company loan. Submit your application to HR with your Department Head's approval.

items.q: I joined 4 months ago. Can I apply?
items.a: No. You must complete six months of active employment.

items.q: I completed 6 months, but I am not confirmed yet. Can I apply?
items.a: No. You must be a confirmed full-time employee.

items.q: Are probationers eligible?
items.a: No. Only confirmed full-time employees are eligible.

items.q: Can interns apply?
items.a: No.

items.q: Can part-time or contract employees apply?
items.a: No. The policy is for confirmed full-time employees.

items.q: Does "six months" mean six months from joining or confirmation?
items.a: Six months of active employment at Petpooja.

items.q: I have an ongoing company loan. Can I get a salary advance?
items.a: No. You are not eligible until your loan is over.

items.q: Can I apply once my loan is over?
items.a: Yes, once your loan balance is cleared, if other conditions are met.

items.q: For what reasons can I get a salary advance?
items.a: Exceptional cases where you face a personal emergency or contingency situation.

items.q: Can I take salary advance for a planned expense?
items.a: No. It cannot be paid where the need is known or predictable.

items.q: Can I take it for a wedding or festival?
items.a: No. These are predictable needs.

items.q: Can I take it for a medical emergency?
items.a: Yes. A sudden medical emergency is an unforeseen contingency.

items.q: Can I take it for a family emergency?
items.a: Yes, in a genuine, unforeseen emergency.

items.q: Can I take salary advance for rent or EMI payments?
items.a: No. These are known and predictable expenses.

items.q: Can I take salary advance for shopping or travel?
items.a: No. It is allowed only for emergencies.

items.q: Who decides if the reason is genuine?
items.a: Your Department Head and HR.

items.q: Do I need to prove my emergency?
items.a: Please provide the reason and any supporting document to your Department Head and HR.

items.q: How much salary advance can I take?
items.a: Not more than 100% of your net monthly salary as per the payroll of the preceding month.

items.q: My net salary last month was Rs. 40,000. What is my maximum advance?
Can I take more than my net salary?
items.a: No. The advance cannot exceed 100% of net monthly salary under any circumstances.

items.q: Is the limit based on gross or net salary?
items.a: On net monthly salary as per the preceding month's payroll.

items.q: Does my attendance matter?
items.a: Yes. The advance is also subject to your attendance record for the month in which you request it.

items.q: I had several LOP days this month. Will it affect the amount?
items.a: Yes, it may. The amount is subject to the attendance record of that month.

items.q: Can I take 50% of my salary as advance?
items.a: Yes. The limit is up to 100% of net monthly salary.

items.q: Can I take 100% of my salary on the 5th of the month?
items.a: The limit is 100% of the preceding month's net salary, subject to attendance and approval.

items.q: How many times can I take a salary advance?
items.a: Up to three times in a calendar year.

items.q: What is the gap between two advances?
items.a: A minimum interval of two months between each request.

items.q: I took an advance in January. Can I take another in February?
items.a: No. A minimum of two months' gap is required.

items.q: I took an advance in January. When can I apply again?
items.a: After a minimum interval of two months, e.g. in March.

items.q: Is the limit per calendar year or financial year?
items.a: Calendar year (January to December).

items.q: Can I take 4 advances in a year?
items.a: No. The maximum is three.

items.q: How will the advance be recovered?
items.a: The entire advance is recovered from the salary payable for the same month.

items.q: Can I repay in installments?
items.a: No. The entire advance is recovered in the same month's salary.

items.q: I took an advance on the 20th of the month. When will it be recovered?
items.a: From that month's salary, which is paid on the payday.

items.q: What will I receive in my next salary?
items.a: The salary for that month less the advance amount already paid.

items.q: What if my advance is more than my salary for that month because of LOP?
items.a: The entire advance is recovered from that month's salary. Please discuss with HR if your salary falls short.

items.q: What happens if I resign after taking an advance?
items.a: The advance is recovered from that month's salary. Any remaining dues are cleared at Full and Final settlement.

items.q: How do I apply?
items.a: Submit an application to the HR department with prior approval from your Department Head.

items.q: Who approves my salary advance?
items.a: Your Department Head approves, HR certifies, and Accounts pays.

items.q: Is my reporting manager's approval enough?
items.a: No. The application requires prior approval from the concerned Department Head.

items.q: What does HR do with my application?
items.a: HR certifies it and forwards it to the Accounts department for payment.

items.q: Who pays the advance?
items.a: The Accounts department, after HR certifies the application.

items.q: How soon will I get the advance?
items.a: The policy does not specify a time. It is processed after approvals and certification.

items.q: Can I apply by phone or WhatsApp?
items.a: No. The application must be submitted to HR with Department Head approval.

items.q: What if my Department Head rejects?
items.a: The advance will not be processed.

items.q: Why do Department Heads recommend this selectively?
items.a: Salary should be paid only on payday, and this facility is for unforeseen circumstances only.

items.q: How many times can I take a salary advance in a year?
items.a: Three times, with at least two months' gap between each.

items.q: How much salary advance can I get?
items.a: Up to 100% of your net monthly salary (previous month), subject to attendance and approval.

items.q: Can I take an advance before Diwali?
items.a: No. It is for emergencies, not for known or predictable needs.

items.q: Can I take an advance for my child's school fees?
items.a: School fees are predictable. A salary advance is not allowed for known needs.

items.q: My father had an accident last night. Can I get a salary advance?
items.a: Yes. This is an unforeseen emergency. Apply to HR with Department Head approval.

items.q: Is salary advance taxable?
items.a: It is part of your salary, which is recovered in the same month. Please check with HR.

items.q: Does the advance affect my PF?
items.a: The advance is recovered from your salary of the same month. Please check with HR/Accounts for PF treatment.

items.q: Can I apply during notice period?
items.a: The policy does not mention it. Please check with HR.

items.q: Can I take a salary advance if I am on LOP?
items.a: It is subject to your attendance record and approval.

items.q: Can I take a salary advance and loan together?
items.a: No. If you have a loan, you cannot take a salary advance until it is over.

items.q: Can I take a loan after a salary advance?
items.a: Under the Loan Policy, you can apply for a loan if you meet the eligibility criteria. A salary advance is recovered in the same month.

items.q: Does the company charge interest on salary advance?
items.a: The policy does not mention any interest.

items.q: Is the policy applicable to all departments?
items.a: Yes, to all confirmed full-time employees.

items.q: Can the company modify this policy?
items.a: Yes, as per business requirements.

items.q: Who do I contact for salary advance?
items.a: The HR department.

items.q: I need money urgently before payday. What can I do?
items.a: If you are a confirmed full-time employee with six months of service and no running loan, apply for a salary advance with Department Head approval, for an unforeseen emergency.

items.q: How do I get my salary before payday?
items.a: Through the Salary Advance facility, in exceptional emergencies, with your Department Head's approval and HR certification.

items.q: What is the minimum gap between two advances?
items.a: Two months.

items.q: Can I take an advance in my first six months?
items.a: No.

items.q: Is the advance paid directly to my bank account?
items.a: Accounts pays the advance after HR certification, as per the normal payment process.

items.q: Is the amount recovered from the salary of the same month or next month?
items.a: The same month.

items.q: What if I request an advance on the last day of the month?
items.a: The advance will be recovered from the same month's salary. Please consult HR on timing.

items.q: Can my team lead approve my advance?
items.a: No. Approval of the concerned Department Head is needed before submission to HR.

items.q: Does HR also approve the advance?
items.a: HR certifies the application after the Department Head's approval and forwards it to Accounts.

items.q: Is an emergency certificate or proof needed?
items.a: The policy does not specify. HR and the Department Head may ask for supporting information.

items.q: Will taking an advance affect my appraisal?
items.a: The policy does not link advance to appraisal.

items.q: Can I take an advance while on notice period?
items.a: The policy does not prohibit it explicitly, but it is allowed only for unforeseen emergencies and is selectively recommended. Please check with HR.

items.q: Does the advance count as a loan under the Loan Policy?
items.a: No. They are separate facilities, but you cannot take a salary advance until a running loan is closed.

items.q: What is a "contingency situation"?
items.a: An unexpected personal emergency, such as a sudden medical or family emergency.

items.q: What does "known or predictable" mean?
items.a: Expenses that you can plan in advance, such as fees, rent, festivals and travel.

items.q: Why was my salary advance rejected?
items.a: It could be because the need was predictable, the Department Head did not recommend it, your attendance record was poor, or you were not eligible.

items.q: Can I appeal if rejected?
items.a: The policy does not provide for an appeal. You can discuss with your Department Head and HR.

items.q: Is the advance limited by my attendance in the month?
items.a: Yes. It is subject to your attendance record for the month in which the advance is requested.

items.q: Can I ask for an advance equal to 1.5 times of my salary?
items.a: No. The maximum is 100% of net monthly salary.

items.q: Can I take a salary advance for buying a laptop?
items.a: No. For a laptop purchase or repair, the Loan Policy may apply.

items.q: Can I take a salary advance for a mobile phone?
items.a: No. The Loan Policy has a provision for mobile handset loan.

items.q: Which is better for a bigger emergency: loan or salary advance?
items.a: A salary advance is capped at 100% of net monthly salary and recovered in the same month. A loan (after 2 years) allows up to 2, 3 or 5 times gross salary with EMIs.

items.q: How many months of service do I need for salary advance versus loan?
items.a: Six months for salary advance, and two years for loan.

items.q: Is the policy applicable to employees working remotely?
items.a: Yes, to all confirmed full-time employees who meet the criteria.

items.q: Is a salary advance part of CTC?
items.a: No. It is an advance of your own salary, recovered in the same month.

items.q: What if I do not get salary in the month due to LOP?
items.a: Salary is first adjusted for LOP and the advance is recovered. Please speak with HR for how such cases are handled.

items.q: Can my family member apply on my behalf?
items.a: No. The employee must apply with Department Head approval.

items.q: Is there an application form?
items.a: The application is submitted to HR. Please ask HR for the format.

items.q: Can I apply for a salary advance by email?
items.a: Please submit the application to HR with the Department Head's approval. Email is generally accepted; confirm with HR.

items.q: What if I am in a different city?
items.a: The same process applies. Submit the application to HR with the Department Head's approval.

items.q: Does it apply if I joined through rehire?
items.a: A rehired employee must meet the six months of active employment condition after rejoining.

items.q: Is there any charge or fee on a salary advance?
items.a: The policy does not mention any fee.

items.q: Is salary advance allowed in the notice period when I have a loan?
items.a: No. Having a loan makes you ineligible until it is over.

items.q: Who is accountable for approving advances selectively?
items.a: The Department Heads.

items.q: What is the Employee Separation Policy?
items.a: It lays down the guidelines for how an employee leaves Petpooja, whether through resignation, end of contract, termination, retrenchment/redundancy or an unforeseen event.

items.q: Who does this policy apply to?
items.a: All full-time and part-time employees, including those appointed on a contract basis.

items.q: What is the effective date?
items.a: 1-04-2023 (Draft Version 1.1).

items.q: What are the types of separation covered?
items.a: Resignation, end of contract, termination of services, retrenchment/redundancy and unforeseen events such as death in service.

items.q: What is resignation?
items.a: A permanent separation from employment that is initiated by the employee.

items.q: How do I resign?
items.a: Submit your resignation in writing (via email) to your Reporting Manager.

items.q: Can I resign verbally?
items.a: No. The resignation must be in writing via email.

items.q: What happens after I submit my resignation?
items.a: Your Reporting Manager shares it by email with the Functional Head and HR. HR and your manager/HOD then talk to you to understand the reason.

items.q: Can I withdraw my resignation?
items.a: Yes. After the discussion, if you choose to stay back, you can withdraw your resignation in writing (via email) with mutual consent.

items.q: What if I decide to continue with my resignation?
items.a: A Resignation Acceptance Letter is issued to you and maintained by HR.

items.q: Can I leave without giving notice?
items.a: No. An employee should not leave or discontinue service without giving prior written notice.

items.q: Who do I give my resignation to?
items.a: Your Reporting Manager.

items.q: Can I send my resignation only to HR?
items.a: The policy says it should be submitted to your Reporting Manager, who shares it with the Functional Head and HR.

items.q: Will HR try to retain me?
items.a: HR and your Reporting Manager/HOD interact with you to understand your reasons, and you may choose to stay back.

items.q: How long is my notice period?
items.a: For confirmed employees, as per your Employment Agreement. For probationary employees, 15 working days.

items.q: Where do I find my notice period?
items.a: In your Employment Agreement or appointment letter.

items.q: When does my notice period start?
items.a: On the date you give your resignation in writing to your Reporting Manager.

items.q: Do I have to serve the full notice period?
items.a: Yes, or pay in lieu the salary for the notice period not served.

items.q: Can I pay and leave early?
items.a: Yes, you can pay the salary for the notice period not served. Management approval and hand-over are still required.

items.q: Can the unserved notice be adjusted against my leave balance?
items.a: Yes. The amount payable for the unserved notice can be adjusted against the amount payable for balance PL.

items.q: Can the company relieve me early?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja can relieve you earlier if you have fulfilled all work commitments. The remaining notice period is waived off.

items.q: I am on probation. What is my notice period?
items.a: 15 working days.

items.q: I am confirmed. Is my notice period 15 working days?
items.a: No. It is as per your Employment Agreement.

items.q: Does the notice period include weekly offs and holidays?
items.a: The probation notice is mentioned in working days. For others, please check your Employment Agreement.

items.q: Who decides my last working day?
items.a: It is mutually decided by your Reporting Manager, HR and you, and approved by the Functional Head.

items.q: What if my last day falls on a holiday?
items.a: You will be relieved on the working day before the holiday.

items.q: Can I choose my last working day on my own?
items.a: No. It is decided jointly and approved by the Functional Head.

items.q: Can I take leave during my notice period?
items.a: No. Employees are not allowed to take any leave during the notice period.

items.q: Is there any exception?
items.a: In exceptional cases (medical or other exigency), you may be allowed to take PL with prior approval from your Reporting Manager.

items.q: What if I take PL during notice?
items.a: Your last working date is extended by the number of leaves availed, at the discretion of the Reporting Manager and Functional Head.

items.q: Will my PL keep accumulating in the notice period?
items.a: Yes. PL accumulates as per the Leave Policy until your last working day.

items.q: Can I take Casual Leave or Sick Leave in my notice period?
items.a: The policy says no leave is allowed in the notice period, except PL in exceptional cases with prior approval.

items.q: What happens when my contract ends?
items.a: A contract that is not extended ends on the date mentioned in the contract.

items.q: When does the contract renewal process start?
items.a: One month before the end of the contract, with performance appraisal and renewal.

items.q: Who decides on contract renewal?
items.a: Your appraiser gives feedback and recommends renewal or end. The Functional Head approves.

items.q: What will I get from HR at contract end?
items.a: A Contract Renewal Letter or a Contract Completion Letter, based on the Functional Head's approval.

items.q: Who can terminate an employee?
items.a: The power to terminate is exercised only by HR.

items.q: On what grounds can I be terminated?
items.a: Violation of the Code of Conduct or the PoSH Policy, or consistently unsatisfactory performance, subject to the policy.

items.q: What happens if I am accused of a code of conduct violation?
items.a: An enquiry is initiated as per the Code of Conduct/PoSH Policy and principles of natural justice, and you get a reasonable opportunity to present your case.

items.q: What if misconduct is proved?
items.a: The company can terminate your services by giving prior notice.

items.q: Can I resign when an enquiry is going on?
items.a: Your resignation will not take effect unless accepted by HR/Director, and you will not be officially relieved until then.

items.q: What are the performance grounds for termination?
items.a: Consistently unsatisfactory or below-expectation performance, unsatisfactory performance after extension of probation, or unsatisfactory evaluation of the Performance Improvement Program (PIP).

items.q: Will I get notice if terminated for performance?
items.a: Yes. The company provides notice or payment in lieu of notice as per the terms of employment.

items.q: Will I get a chance to improve before termination?
items.a: Termination may follow after extension of probation or PIP evaluation. It is based on performance.

items.q: What is retrenchment or redundancy?
items.a: Separation for reasons not relating to an employee's performance or behaviour, such as restructuring or phase out of departments for strategic reasons.

items.q: Will I get notice in retrenchment?
items.a: Yes. The company provides notice or payment in lieu of notice as per the terms of employment.

items.q: Who decides on retrenchment?
items.a: Management, at its discretion.

items.q: What support does the company give in case of an employee's death?
items.a: HR, along with the Functional Head and Director's approval, supports the family, including an advance to the next of kin.

items.q: Will the family get an advance?
items.a: Yes, if required, to take care of immediate expenses.

items.q: How soon is the Full and Final settlement made in case of death?
items.a: Within 7 working days, from which the advance is adjusted.

items.q: What other benefits are processed?
items.a: PF, Gratuity, Medical-claim cover and other statutory benefits, processed expeditiously.

items.q: What do I need to do before leaving?
items.a: Complete your work and commitments, settle all dues, return company property, and complete the Exit Clearance & Interview Form.

items.q: What company property must I return?
items.a: Laptops, desktops, printers, data cards, stationery, cabinet keys, ID cards, library books and any files or documents.

items.q: To whom do I hand over the files?
items.a: To your Reporting Manager.

items.q: What dues do I have to clear?
items.a: All amounts due to Petpooja, including loans and advances.

items.q: What if I have a pending loan?
items.a: The entire outstanding becomes due, and it is recovered before your separation. The relieving letter is withheld until dues are cleared.

items.q: Will I get my relieving letter?
items.a: Yes, if you settle all dues before leaving.

items.q: Will I get my experience certificate?
items.a: Yes, only if you settle all dues before discharge from Petpooja.

items.q: What if I do not return my laptop?
items.a: Your relieving letter and experience certificate will not be issued, and the amount may be adjusted in your FnF.

items.q: What is the Exit Clearance & Interview Form?
items.a: A form that you complete and submit to HR before leaving.

items.q: When will I receive my Full and Final settlement?
items.a: Within 45 working days after your exit.

items.q: When will I get my last month's salary?
items.a: Along with the Full and Final settlement, within 45 working days after your exit.

items.q: What if I worked less than 15 days in my last month?
items.a: Your last 2 months' salary will be paid together with the Full and Final settlement.

items.q: What is included in my Full and Final settlement?
items.a: Monthly pay until your last working day, unclaimed salary reimbursements and expenses, PL encashment, performance incentive (if applicable), and gratuity (if applicable), on a pro-rata basis.

items.q: Will I get PL encashment?
items.a: Yes, as per the Leave Policy, on your last drawn basic salary, up to the limit.

items.q: Will I get my performance incentive after I leave?
items.a: Only if you are on the rolls of Petpooja on the date when incentives are disbursed.

items.q: Will I get gratuity?
items.a: If you are eligible under applicable law.

items.q: Will deductions be made from my final settlement?
items.a: Yes. The net amount is paid after adjusting deductions and recoveries.

items.q: Will the company help me with my PF?
items.a: Yes. Petpooja provides assistance for settlement or transfer of Provident Fund.

items.q: Do I have to go through an exit interview?
items.a: Yes. Every separating employee goes through an exit interview.

items.q: Who conducts the exit interview?
items.a: HR initiates and completes the process.

items.q: Why is there an exit interview?
items.a: To understand your experience at Petpooja and the reasons for resignation, and to plan improvements.

items.q: Do I need to fill in a form?
items.a: Yes, the exit interview form, which you hand over to HR.

items.q: Do I need to give my contact details?
items.a: Yes. Separating employees must provide contact details and addresses for future correspondence.

items.q: I want to resign. What should I do?
items.a: Send your resignation by email to your Reporting Manager. He/she shares it with your Functional Head and HR, who will talk to you. If you continue, you get a Resignation Acceptance Letter.

items.q: What is the notice period for a probationer?
items.a: 15 working days.

items.q: Can I buy out my notice period?
items.a: You can pay the salary in lieu for the notice period not served, subject to approval.

items.q: How is notice pay calculated?
items.a: The policy says "salary for the notice period not served". HR calculates it from your salary.

items.q: Can my PL balance be used to cover the notice shortfall?
items.a: Yes. The amount payable for unserved notice can be adjusted against PL balance payable.

items.q: Can the company ask me to leave earlier than my notice period?
items.a: Yes, if you have fulfilled all work commitments, the company may relieve you earlier and waive the remaining period.

items.q: If I am relieved earlier, do I still need to pay for notice?
items.a: No. The remaining notice period is waived off.

items.q: Who approves my last working day?
items.a: The Functional Head.

items.q: I am sick during my notice period. What should I do?
items.a: In exceptional cases (medical exigency), you may be allowed PL with prior approval from your Reporting Manager. Your last working day will be extended by the days of leave.

items.q: Will my last working day change if I take PL?
items.a: Yes. It is extended by the number of leaves availed.

items.q: Can my resignation be rejected?
items.a: The policy talks about acceptance. For employees under enquiry, resignation does not take effect until accepted by HR/Director.

items.q: Can I resign while on a PIP?
items.a: The policy does not prohibit it. HR and your manager will discuss your reasons.

items.q: What happens if I abandon my job?
items.a: Under the Leave and Attendance Policies, it is treated as withdrawal of service, and the Rehire Policy lists job abandonment as non-eligible for rehire.

items.q: Will I get my salary for the notice period if I serve it?
items.a: Yes. You get monthly remuneration till your last working day.

items.q: Will my PL be encashed at the time of exit?
items.a: Yes, on your last drawn basic salary, as per the Leave Policy.

items.q: Is leave encashment given for CL or SL?
items.a: No. Only PL is encashable.

items.q: When will I get my relieving letter?
items.a: After you settle all dues and complete exit formalities.

items.q: Can I get an experience letter without clearing dues?
items.a: No. It is issued only if all dues are settled.

items.q: How long will my FnF take?
items.a: Within 45 working days after your exit.

items.q: What is the FnF timeline in case of an employee's death?
items.a: Within 7 working days.

items.q: What if I worked 10 days in my last month?
items.a: The last 2 months' salary will be paid along with the Full and Final settlement.

items.q: What if I worked 20 days in my last month?
items.a: Your last month's salary is paid along with the Full and Final settlement.

items.q: Will unpaid reimbursements be paid?
items.a: Yes, unclaimed salary reimbursements and expenses are included in the FnF.

items.q: What happens to my performance incentive if I resign before payout?
items.a: It is paid only if you are on the rolls on the date of disbursement.

items.q: What if I have taken a salary advance?
items.a: Dues such as advances must be settled prior to separation.

items.q: Will the company transfer my PF?
items.a: The company assists with PF settlement or transfer.

items.q: Can I take a Loan during my notice period?
items.a: The Loan Policy applies to confirmed employees in good standing. If you leave, the entire outstanding is due.

items.q: What is the role of the Functional Head in separation?
items.a: The Functional Head receives the resignation, approves the last working day and, for contracts, approves extension or termination.

items.q: What is a Contract Completion Letter?
items.a: A letter issued by HR when a contract ends and is not renewed.

items.q: What is the Resignation Acceptance Letter?
items.a: A letter issued by HR acknowledging your resignation after discussions.

items.q: What if I do not complete the Exit Clearance form?
items.a: It is a required step. Your relieving letter and settlement may be affected.

items.q: Do part-time employees also follow this?
items.a: Yes. The policy covers full-time, part-time and contract employees.

items.q: Can termination happen without any inquiry?
items.a: For code of conduct or PoSH violations, an enquiry is initiated as per natural justice. Performance-based termination follows the PIP or probation evaluation process.

items.q: Who decides on termination?
items.a: Only HR exercises the power to terminate.
